CVE-2026-91141.desc: A vulnerability in the default configuration of vsomeip allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to trigger massive memory allocations by sending a small TCP packet with a large, attacker-declared SOME/IP length field. This can lead to immediate service termination via OOM-kill on memory-constrained systems or total host memory exhaustion through repeated connections.
CVE-2026-91141.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-120868.desc: Memory overflow in Packet Processing can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or Denial of Service in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway.

CVE-2026-126355.desc: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. Prior to 4.13.16, csrf() limits origin validation to the content types normally sent by HTML forms and therefore does not validate text/ping requests generated by Chromium hyperlink auditing. Chrome and Edge can send a cross-origin credentialed POST without a CORS preflight through an <a ping> action, and the middleware then skips both Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checks. The fixed request body limits exploitation to state-changing endpoints whose effect is selected by the path or query string and does not depend on submitted body data. The user's cookie must accompany the request, which generally requires a same-site origin or a cookie configured with SameSite=None, and Firefox does not send hyperlink-auditing pings by default. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.
CVE-2026-126355.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126356.desc: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 4.5.1 until 4.13.16, validator('form') uses a strict whole-header pattern that fails to recognize multipart/form-data when its Content-Type includes another legal parameter or extra whitespace after a semicolon. The validation callback receives an empty object even though c.req.parseBody() or c.req.formData() can still parse and expose all submitted fields to the handler. An unauthenticated client can therefore bypass allow-list or required-field checks when the application relies on the form validator and its callback accepts an empty object. application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.
CVE-2026-126356.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126357.desc: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. Prior to 4.13.16, mount() and app.mount() can remove a dynamic mount prefix using the route-pattern length rather than the matched-prefix length, allowing a crafted path to be forwarded as a protected inner route while the outer application routes the original path. Since 4.12.21, rebuilding the forwarded URL from the decoded pathname can also convert a decoded backslash to a slash and collapse parent-directory segments, again causing the mounted application to receive a protected path. An unauthenticated client can use either applicable path transformation to reach a mounted route without authentication or authorization middleware scoped to a subpath inside the mount prefix. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.
CVE-2026-126357.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126358.desc: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 4.1.4 until 4.13.16, RegExpRouter can omit wildcard middleware in three version-specific cases: since 4.13.0, middleware using the explicit default parameter pattern in /api/:tenant{[^/]+}/admin/* is not applied to a route written as /api/:tenant/admin/:id; since 4.1.4, middleware on /admin/* is not applied to a route registered as /admin* for paths under /admin/; and since 4.4.0, a request path containing an encoded line terminator can reach the not-found handler without wildcard middleware. The default SmartRouter selects RegExpRouter for most applications, and the router's registration-time coverage calculation treated the first two matching pattern pairs as different while its compiled wildcard did not match line terminators in the third case. An unauthenticated client can reach a route handler or the not-found handler without authentication or authorization middleware registered on the wildcard path. TrieRouter, LinearRouter, and PatternRouter apply the middleware in the three described cases. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.
CVE-2026-126358.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126359.desc: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 3.12.0 until 4.13.16, the css helper in hono/css escapes interpolated string values separately and therefore fails to neutralize a closing style tag when < ends the template text or a preceding value and / begins the next attacker-controlled value. During server-side rendering, the combined output can close the <Style /> element early and cause the remainder of the interpolated value to be interpreted as HTML. Applications that place an untrusted string immediately after < in a css template, including adjacent untrusted interpolations, can expose viewers to attacker-controlled HTML or script and information accessible to that page. Other uses of the css helper are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.
CVE-2026-126359.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126360.desc: OpenTelemetry Python provides the Python API and SDK for OpenTelemetry. Prior to 1.45.2, TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract() in opentelemetry-api can perform quadratic-time regular-expression backtracking on a malformed traceparent value containing a trace-context prefix, a long whitespace sequence, and an embedded newline. Exploitation requires an attacker-controlled carrier that preserves embedded newlines and permits a sufficiently large value, because conforming HTTP header values cannot contain embedded newlines. JSON-based carriers, including applicable MCP request metadata integrations, can preserve the required newline depending on the SDK, instrumentation, and message-size limits. Parsing on an asynchronous server's event-loop thread can consume excessive CPU and delay unrelated requests, while the advisory does not establish disclosure, modification, or code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.45.2.
CVE-2026-126360.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126361.desc: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to 7.4.5, Astro rendered a string used as a dynamic element name as raw HTML after applying an incomplete character filter. A / in the string could make an HTML parser treat the remainder as attributes, allowing untrusted element-name input to inject event-handler markup. The .astro dynamic-tag renderer, JSX renderer, and MDX renderer were affected, and exploitation required an application to use request-controlled or stored untrusted data as all or part of an element name. This issue is fixed in version 7.4.5.
CVE-2026-126361.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126362.desc: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.7.3 until 9.1.2, the @astrojs/svelte renderer inserted a named slot into the quoted name attribute of an astro-slot wrapper without HTML escaping. Request-controlled slot names containing a quote could terminate the attribute and inject active HTML. Exploitation required a hydrated Svelte component using a client:* directive and dynamic rendering of the attacker-chosen slot; components that did not render that slot emitted only Astro's escaped fallback content. Both server rendering and client-side hydration used the unsafe slot name. This issue is fixed in version 9.1.2.
CVE-2026-126362.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126363.desc: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 0.2.0 until 7.1.2, the @astrojs/solid-js renderer inserted a named slot into the quoted name attribute of an astro-slot wrapper without HTML escaping. A request-controlled slot name containing a quote could terminate the attribute and inject active HTML. Exploitation required a hydrated Solid component using a client:* directive and dynamic access to the attacker-chosen slot property; a component that did not render that slot emitted only escaped fallback content. This issue is fixed in version 7.1.2.
CVE-2026-126363.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126364.desc: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.14.3 until 7.4.7, Astro's /_image endpoint compared the requested local-image path with the build output directory without preserving case on case-sensitive filesystems. A sibling directory whose path differed from the output directory only by letter case could therefore pass the containment check, allowing an unauthenticated requester to read image files accepted by the image service from outside the output directory. Exploitation required on-demand rendering with the @astrojs/node adapter, a case-sensitive filesystem, and a preexisting case-variant sibling directory; ordinary traversal to unrelated paths was already rejected. This issue is fixed in Astro version 7.4.7.
CVE-2026-126364.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126365.desc: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to @astrojs/prism 4.1.2, and from @astrojs/markdoc 0.3.0 until 2.1.2, runHighlighterWithAstro() returned code unchanged when Prism had no grammar for the requested language, and callers inserted that result as raw HTML. A code block labeled with an unsupported language could therefore render embedded HTML and script instead of displaying it as text. The Prism component was affected when applications supplied untrusted code with an unsupported or attacker-controlled lang, and the @astrojs/markdoc prism() extension was affected for less-trusted content authors even when Markdoc's ordinary HTML rendering was disabled. This issue is fixed in @astrojs/prism 4.1.2 and @astrojs/markdoc 2.1.2.
CVE-2026-126365.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126367.desc: @grpc/grpc-js implements the core functionality of gRPC purely in JavaScript, without a C++ addon. Before 1.13.2, and from 1.14.0 through 1.14.1, the @grpc/grpc-js-xds SafeRegexValueMatcher and PathSafeRegexValueMatcher add start and end anchors without grouping a supplied top-level alternation. An expression intended to match one of several complete values can therefore match a prefix, substring, or suffix. The affected matchers are used for route selection, xDS credential identity matching, and RBAC URL path, principal name, server name, and header rules. An ALLOW policy using an alternation can consequently accept a method, certificate identity, or header value outside the intended set, while a DENY policy becomes broader rather than permissive. This issue is fixed in versions 1.13.2 and 1.14.2.
CVE-2026-126367.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126792.desc: A memory-safety flaw in the key-management request-building component of the library can lead to an out-of-bounds write on the heap. A fixed-size output buffer is used under an assumption about cryptographic key size that is never validated, so when the library is embedded by a caller that supplies its own cryptographic callback implementation, data larger than the buffer can be written past its end. Exploitation requires the ability to control the embedding application's in-process key-management provider configuration, a high-privilege position. The demonstrated impact is memory corruption resulting in abnormal termination of the client process.
CVE-2026-126792.path: local access needed, needs admin rights, no user action

CVE-2026-126839.desc: A deserialization type-restriction control in the BSON serialization component can be bypassed because the check used to recognize a class of compiler-generated types relies on an overly permissive heuristic rather than a precise identification. An unauthorized party able to supply BSON content that an application later deserializes into a loosely typed member can cause types outside the intended allow-list to be constructed and populated with unauthorized party-supplied values inside the consuming application. This can lead to unexpected object state and errors in downstream application logic. No elevated privileges beyond the ability to place unauthorized party-influenced content in the deserialization path are required.
CVE-2026-126839.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126982.title: Remote code execution via generic-type allow-list bypass in BSON object deserialization
CVE-2026-126982.desc: A type allow-list bypass in the BSON serialization library of the MongoDB C# Driver allows a type-restriction check to be circumvented when polymorphic data is deserialized into loosely typed members. An unauthorized party who can supply or plant BSON/JSON data that the application later deserializes can cause the application process to instantiate .NET types outside the intended allow-list and populate them with unauthorized party-controlled values. In applications that contain a suitable gadget type, this can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the application, with corresponding loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability. No special privileges beyond the ability to introduce data the application reads are required.
CVE-2026-126982.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-127212.desc: Dokploy before 0.31.1 contains a missing ownership check vulnerability in the readAppMonitoring tRPC procedure that allows authenticated attackers to access container metrics belonging to other organizations by supplying an arbitrary appName. Attackers can query getApplicationStats with any application name, including the fixed "dokploy" control-plane service name, to read CPU, memory, network I/O, and block I/O metrics for containers they do not own on self-hosted multi-tenant instances.
CVE-2026-127212.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-128065.desc: @grpc/grpc-js implements the core functionality of gRPC purely in JavaScript, without a C++ addon. From 1.14.0 through 1.14.1, XdsServer in @grpc/grpc-js-xds can acknowledge Route and VirtualHost resources while failing to apply their RBACPerRoute override configurations. The override parser is not registered under the override message type, override maps are stored under a type URL instead of the configured HTTP filter name, and VirtualHost override maps are not read. When experimental RBAC is enabled and a trusted xDS control plane supplies a broad top-level ALLOW policy with a stricter matching override, affected servers evaluate RPCs under the broad policy and can accept requests that should be denied. This issue is fixed in version 1.14.2.
CVE-2026-128065.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-128066.title: Pillow: Memory DoS in TIFF and EXIF IFD parsing via overlapping tag data
CVE-2026-128066.desc: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 1.0 through 12.3.0, ImageFileDirectory_v2.load() in src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py retains a separate bytes object for each out-of-line IFD tag value without limiting the total data read or preventing distinct tags from referencing the same file region. A small crafted TIFF or EXIF-bearing JPEG, PNG, WebP, or MPO can therefore cause memory use quadratic in the input size. TIFF and some JPEG paths trigger parsing during Image.open(), while other formats are exposed when EXIF is requested, including through getexif() or ImageOps.exif_transpose(). The declared pixel dimensions do not bound this metadata allocation, so decompression-bomb checks do not prevent process memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.
CVE-2026-128066.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-92735.desc: HashiCorp Vault and Vault Enterprise are vulnerable to an issue in the integrated storage join process that may allow an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a new, uninitialized node to cause that node to send credentials from its server environment to an attacker-controlled server. CVE-2026-127915.desc:
The MCUboot TLV iterator bootutil_tlv_iter_next() in boot/bootutil/src/tlv.c walks image trailer TLVs with a single loop guard (it->tlv_off < it->tlv_end) and advances by sizeof(struct image_tlv) + tlv.it_len using the attacker-controlled it_len field, without validating that the entry's header or payload stays within it->tlv_end. As a result the 4-byte header read can extend up to 3 bytes past the declared TLV area, and the returned (off, len) can describe a payload that runs past it.

The path is pre-authentication: TLVs are parsed during bootutil_img_validate() before the signature is verified, and a crafted image can be presented through DFU / serial-recovery / OTA. However the impact is contained by surrounding guards: bootutil_img_validate() first rejects a TLV area larger than bootutil_max_image_size(), the default LOAD_IMAGE_DATA sink is flash_area_read() which bounds-checks against the flash partition and fails an out-of-partition read, and every payload consumer (EXPECTED_HASH_TLV, EXPECTED_KEY_TLV, EXPECTED_SIG_TLV, IMAGE_TLV_SEC_CNT) clamps len against a fixed buffer before copying.

The residual effect in a default flash build is therefore an out-of-region read confined to the attacker's own slot partition whose result is never observable, yielding at worst a clean validation failure rather than memory corruption or information disclosure. A genuine (though still bounded) out-of-bounds read remains under the non-default MCUBOOT_RAM_LOAD configuration, where LOAD_IMAGE_DATA is an unchecked memcpy. The fix is to validate each entry's header and payload against it->tlv_end inside the iterator.
CVE-2026-127915.path: physical access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-127916.desc:
bootutil_img_hash() computes the image digest over ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size + ih_protect_tlv_size bytes, all three taken from the candidate image's header, and reads that span out of the slot without checking that it fits in the flash area. The three sizes are also summed without an overflow check. Nothing earlier on the validation path bounds the whole span either: bootutil_img_validate() compares the image size against bootutil_max_image_size() only after the hash has been computed.

The callers bound part of the span, or none of it:

On the swap and overwrite upgrade path, boot_validate_slot() first runs the image header check (boot_is_header_valid(), later boot_check_header_valid()). Before MCUboot 2.2.0 that check covered only ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size, so for every image the protected-TLV area (ih_protect_tlv_size, a uint16_t, up to 65535 bytes) was hashed without being bounded. From 2.2.0 the check includes ih_protect_tlv_size, except for a compressed image in the secondary slot when MCUBOOT_DECOMPRESS_IMAGES (CONFIG_BOOT_DECOMPRESSION) is enabled, which leaves the same gap of up to 64 KB.
Zephyr's single-slot and firmware loaders (boot/zephyr/single_loader.c, boot/zephyr/firmware_loader.c) read the header with boot_image_load_header(), which bounds ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size against the flash area. Before MCUboot 2.4.0 that bound did not include ih_protect_tlv_size, which leaves the same gap of up to 64 KB. From 2.4.0 these loaders bound the whole span.
The serial recovery image-list and image-state handlers (bs_list() and bs_set() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c) call bootutil_img_validate() with no header check at all, so on those paths ih_img_size is unbounded as well.

The image is hashed before its signature is checked, so anyone who can place an image in a slot (an OTA or SMP update delivered through the application, or serial recovery) reaches this read before authentication.

Whether a malformed header produces an actual read beyond the area depends on the flash backend:

Backends whose flash_area_read() bounds-checks the request (Zephyr, Espressif, NuttX, Mbed) return an error once the chunked read crosses the end of the area. Validation fails and the image is rejected, with no over-read.
With MCUBOOT_HASH_STORAGE_DIRECTLY (Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_IMG_HASH_DIRECTLY_ON_STORAGE, available from 2.2.0, not enabled by default) the span is hashed through a single direct pointer into memory-mapped flash, with no bounds check.
The Cypress PSoC6 port's flash_area_read() (boot/cypress/cy_flash_pal/cy_flash_map.c, from 1.6.0) does not bound the read: its assert()s compare against the area's absolute offset rather than its size, and it copies with memcpy().

The bytes read past the area feed only the digest, which is compared internally and never returned, so nothing is disclosed. The realistic effect is a read fault during image validation: up to 64 KB past the slot on the upgrade path and, before 2.4.0, on the Zephyr loaders, and potentially much further on the serial recovery handlers, which skip the header check. Where validation is repeated at every boot (a pending upgrade, or, before 2.4.0, the single-slot loader checking its image), the fault can recur on each reset and keep the device from booting.

The fix makes bootutil_img_hash() add the three sizes with boot_u32_safe_add() and reject an image whose span, including the sector offset used in swap-using-offset mode, does not fit in the flash area, before any of it is hashed. Because the bound is applied where the bytes are read, it covers every caller.
CVE-2026-127916.path: local access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-127928.desc:
In MCUboot's serial-recovery encrypted-image support (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c), decrypt_image_inplace() and boot_image_validate_encrypted() each keep a stack-local struct boot_status. boot_enc_load() writes the plaintext per-image AES key into its enckey[] field. Neither function cleared this structure before returning. In addition, a decrypt failure inside the per-sector loop of decrypt_image_inplace() returned early and skipped the total_out: cleanup, which left the expanded AES key context (enc_data) on the stack as well. The error paths of boot_image_validate_encrypted() similarly skipped boot_enc_zeroize().

The affected code is built when encrypted images (MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES, Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_ENCRYPT_IMAGE) are combined with serial recovery. It runs when an encrypted image is uploaded to the primary slot over the recovery protocol, and when the image list or state is queried while an encrypted image is in the secondary slot. After these functions return, the image's AES content key remains in dead stack memory. An attacker who can later read device RAM, for example through a debug port or retained RAM, can recover it.

This weakens the confidentiality of image-encryption keys within the bootloader trust boundary. A recovered key exposes the plaintext of the encrypted firmware image it protects. The device's long-term private decryption key is not exposed. No remote or recovery-protocol channel that returns this memory is known, so exploitation requires a separate memory-read capability.
CVE-2026-127928.path: physical access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-128091.desc:
When MCUboot is built with the TinyCrypt crypto backend (MCUBOOT_USE_TINYCRYPT), bootutil_aes_ctr_drop() in boot/bootutil/include/bootutil/crypto/aes_ctr_tinycrypt.h was an empty stub. The AES-CTR context for this backend is the fully expanded AES-128 key schedule (struct tc_aes_key_sched_struct). Generic code relies on this hook to release and clear key state, so with TinyCrypt nothing was cleared. The mbedTLS and PSA backends do free or destroy their key state here.

As a result, boot_state_clear(), which boot_go() calls before handing off to the application, left the image's AES content-encryption key schedule in the static boot_data state. This is the case after an encrypted upgrade in single-image builds, where boot_enc_zeroize() is not called. boot_decrypt_key() likewise left the ECIES-derived key-encryption key schedule on the stack. The affected build uses MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES with TinyCrypt, which is the default ECDSA and Ed25519 backend in the Zephyr port.

The first AES-128 round key equals the cipher key, so anyone who can read the leftover bootloader RAM after boot can recover the image content key and decrypt that encrypted image. That includes a physical attacker with debug or RAM access, or code later running on the device. This weakens image-encryption key confidentiality (and so the confidentiality of the encrypted image's plaintext). The device's long-term private decryption key is not exposed, and image authenticity is not affected. The fix wipes the context with bootutil_wipe_memory().
CVE-2026-128091.path: physical access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-16659.desc:
MCUboot's serial-recovery image-upload handler bs_upload() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c declares const struct flash_area *fap = NULL and assigns it only via flash_area_open() part-way through the function. Two early validation failures (goto out_invalid_data) — a CBOR map that fails to decode, or an upload packet missing the off/data members — branch past the open while fap is still NULL, then fall into the shared epilogue. In MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES builds that epilogue unconditionally calls boot_handle_enc_fw(fap), which reaches boot_image_load_header() and flash_area_read() and dereferences the NULL flash_area.

The defect is reachable pre-authentication: the trigger is the very first serial-recovery upload command carrying a malformed payload. The guarding conditions are default-true on a fresh recovery session — img_num, curr_off and img_size are zero-initialized statics, so curr_off == img_size and the primary-slot test both hold. It requires a non-default build: encrypted images (MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES / Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_ENCRYPT_IMAGE) together with an active serial-recovery transport, on the Zephyr or Mynewt port (the two that build both boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c and boot_serial_encryption.c with MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES).

The impact is a transient denial of service of the bootloader during recovery. fap is a hard NULL rather than an attacker-controlled value, so there is no memory-corruption or information-leak primitive and image authentication is unaffected. Whether the dereference faults is platform-dependent — on targets where address 0x0 is mapped readable flash the read merely returns an error and execution continues, while targets that trap NULL (MPU / null-pointer-exception detection) take a hard fault. Because serial recovery is unauthenticated by design and already permits the console attacker to write the secondary slot, the added capability is only a low-value transient crash.

The related unconditional flash_area_close(fap) call in the same epilogue is a safe no-op on the ports that reach it, so it does not contribute to the dereference.

The affected ports are the Zephyr port — boot/zephyr/CMakeLists.txt compiles boot_serial.c under CONFIG_MCUBOOT_SERIAL and boot_serial_encryption.c under CONFIG_BOOT_ENCRYPT_IMAGE — and the Mynewt port, whose mcuboot_config.h defines MCUBOOT_SERIAL unconditionally and MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES under any BOOTUTIL_ENCRYPT_ syscfg, with boot/boot_serial/pkg.yml declaring no explicit source list so the whole directory is built. The Espressif port is not affected**: it compiles boot_serial.c but not boot_serial_encryption.c, and defines no MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES, so the #ifdef MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES block containing the call is preprocessed away. The NuttX, Cypress and Mbed ports do not build boot_serial.c at all.
CVE-2026-16659.path: local access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-16662.desc:
boot_save_boot_status() in boot/bootutil/src/boot_record.c reads the image's EXPECTED_HASH_TLV into a stack buffer image_hash[IMAGE_HASH_SIZE] that is never zero-initialised. The TLV handler validates only the upper bound (len > sizeof(image_hash)) and then reads exactly len bytes, so a TLV shorter than IMAGE_HASH_SIZE leaves the tail of image_hash holding stale stack content. The subsequent copy into the boot record, memcpy(buf + offset, image_hash, sizeof(image_hash)), uses the fixed buffer size rather than len, so up to IMAGE_HASH_SIZE - 1 bytes of uninitialised bootloader stack are written into the measured-boot record.

The defect is reachable only under MCUBOOT_MEASURED_BOOT, and only when nothing has checked the length of the hash TLV before boot_save_boot_status() reads it. bootutil_img_validate() rejects a hash TLV whose length is not exactly sizeof(hash) (boot/bootutil/src/image_validate.c:345), and primary-slot validation is on by default (Zephyr's CONFIG_BOOT_VALIDATE_SLOT0 defaults to y), so in a default build the malformed image never reaches this code. Two kinds of build let a short TLV through:

Builds that use pure signatures (MCUBOOT_SIGN_PURE, Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_SIGNATURE_TYPE_PURE). The signature covers the image itself, so the hash-TLV check in bootutil_img_validate() is compiled out, and a pure-signed image normally carries no hash TLV. A hash TLV is still allowed in the unprotected TLV area, which the signature does not cover, so a short one can be added to a correctly signed image without invalidating it. This applies with every upgrade strategy, including direct-XIP and RAM-load, and the modified image can be delivered through any path that accepts a signed image.
Builds with primary-slot validation turned off: the swap and overwrite loader built without MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT, which checks only the image magic before calling boot_add_shared_data(), and the Zephyr single-slot loader (boot/zephyr/single_loader.c) built without it, including the MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT_ONCE variant, which skips validation once the trailer records an earlier successful one. Placing the crafted image requires physical or flash-write access to the device; in a single-slot build with serial recovery enabled, the serial-recovery upload writes the primary slot directly and can place it as well. Outside pure-signature builds, the direct-XIP and RAM-load strategies in boot/bootutil/src/loader.c validate the selected slot unconditionally and are not affected.

It is also reachable through a time-of-check/time-of-use change to tamperable external flash between validation and the boot-record read.

In these configurations the boot record's measurement is already not trustworthy: the hash copied into the record is the image's own EXPECTED_HASH_TLV, which nothing has verified and which the attacker chooses. The defect therefore does not weaken attestation integrity any further. What it adds is a path for bootloader memory to leave the device: up to 63 bytes (IMAGE_HASH_SIZE - 1) of uninitialised bootloader stack are embedded in the measurement field that a downstream attestation service sends to a remote verifier. In the configurations analysed the residue is bootloader internal state (TLV offsets and lengths, flash addresses, loop state), not key material, but what occupies that stack region depends on configuration and on which code ran before boot_save_boot_status(). It is reported as a low-severity, defense-in-depth disclosure with no integrity or availability impact.

This is distinct from the already-fixed record_len integer underflow in the same routine (GHSA-8hrv-4cp5-4rg3). The fix rejects any EXPECTED_HASH_TLV whose length is not exactly IMAGE_HASH_SIZE.
CVE-2026-16662.path: physical access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-16664.desc:
MCUboot's Zephyr serial-recovery upload handler bs_upload() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c decodes the host-supplied image field of an MCUmgr image-upload request into img_num (a full 32-bit value) and latches it on the off == 0 packet without any range check. It then passes img_num straight to flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0), which on the Zephyr port resolves to __flash_area_ids_for_slot() in boot/zephyr/include/sysflash/sysflash.h and indexes the static const int all_slots[] table as all_slots[img_num  2]. That table holds only MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER  2 entries, so any img_num >= MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER is an out-of-bounds read.

The path is reachable by anyone with access to the serial / SMP recovery console, which is unauthenticated by design, and the bad value is supplied before any image signature is verified. The defect is specific to the default non-direct upload path (MCUBOOT_SERIAL_DIRECT_IMAGE_UPLOAD disabled) on the Zephyr port with the array-backed slot layout (not CONFIG_SINGLE_APPLICATION_SLOT). It is not gated on a multi-image configuration: MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER defaults to 1, so even a default single-image build is affected for any image >= 1. The MCUBOOT_SERIAL_DIRECT_IMAGE_UPLOAD path is safe (its flash_area_id_from_direct_image() switch returns -EINVAL for unknown indices).

flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot() takes a signed int image_index while img_num is uint32_t, so the attacker controls the sign of the index as well as its magnitude: an image of 0xFFFFFFFE converts to -2 and reads all_slots[-4], off the front of the table, while large positive values read off the end (CWE-192). (0xFFFFFFFF itself is the "no image given" sentinel and selects image 0.) Either way the index multiply img * 2 is performed in int, so a wild offset yields a bus/hard fault, giving a reliable denial of service of the bootloader during recovery. For moderately out-of-range indices the read returns adjacent .rodata as a garbage flash-area id that is handed to flash_area_open(); this normally fails with MGMT_ERR_EINVAL, but if the garbage id happens to match a valid non-image partition, the subsequent erase/write can target a partition outside the image set (CWE-787). The attacker-supplied value is never echoed back, so there is no information disclosure. The fix is to reject img_num >= BOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER on the off == 0 packet, before the slot lookup. The comparison must be made on the unsigned img_num: an equivalent guard applied after the conversion to int would not reject the negative case above. __flash_area_ids_for_slot() should bounds-check its own arguments as defence in depth.
This vulnerability was reported independently twice: by NVIDIA Project Vanessa on 2026-06-22, and by Kai Phan (@kaimandalic) on 2026-07-19 as GHSA-8v33-88p6-jffj, which is closed as a duplicate of this advisory. Both original reports are reproduced in full below.
CVE-2026-16664.path: local access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-16671.desc:
split_image_check() in boot/bootutil/src/loader.c declares a fixed uint8_t loader_hash[32] buffer and passes it as the out_hash out-parameter to bootutil_img_validate(). That routine copies IMAGE_HASH_SIZE bytes into out_hash (memcpy(out_hash, hash, IMAGE_HASH_SIZE) in boot/bootutil/src/image_validate.c), where IMAGE_HASH_SIZE is a compile-time constant of 64 for MCUBOOT_SHA512 or 48 for MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC384/SHA-384 (boot/bootutil/include/bootutil/crypto/sha.h). The buffer tracks SHA-256 (32 bytes) while the copy length tracks the configured algorithm, so the write overruns the buffer by 16 or 32 bytes.

The overflow is only present in a non-default configuration: the legacy Mynewt split-image feature must be compiled (split_go()/split_image_check(), i.e. neither MCUBOOT_DIRECT_XIP nor MCUBOOT_RAM_LOAD), the digest must be larger than 32 bytes (MCUBOOT_SHA512 or MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC384), and MCUBOOT_SIGN_PURE must be off. split_go() is a public API with no caller inside MCUboot; it is invoked from a Mynewt application. In the default SHA-256 build there is no overflow.

The over-written bytes are the one-way digest of the loader image and the overflow length is fixed at build time, so the contents are not meaningfully attacker-controlled and the size is not attacker-chosen. The realistic impact is bounded, uncontrolled corruption of the bootloader's stack on the split-boot path, manifesting as instability or failed boot in the affected configuration rather than reliable code execution. The fix is to size loader_hash to IMAGE_HASH_SIZE and pass IMAGE_HASH_SIZE as the matching seed length.
CVE-2026-16671.path: local access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-128424.desc: A flaw was found in Kroxylicious. The ACL authorizer's rules-file parser unquotes `matching /…/` regular-expression literals using the string unquoting rules, which strips every backslash escape. As a result, an allow rule such as `matching /orders\.v1/` is compiled as the regex `orders.v1`, which also matches unintended names such as `ordersXv1`, and character classes such as `\d` and `\w` lose their special meaning. Allow rules written with regex escapes can therefore apply to more resources than the author intended. Depending on the ACL configuration, this may allow an authenticated Kafka client to access a resource (such as read or write a topic) that should have been denied.

CVE-2026-128637.desc: The MISP Modules website component contains an open redirect vulnerability in its login endpoint. The /login route accepted a user-supplied next query parameter and passed it directly to Flask's redirect() function without validating the destination. An attacker could craft a URL such as https://victim-host/login?next=https://attacker.example/phish and deliver it to a user (e.g., via email or a lookalike page). After the user successfully authenticated, the application issued a 302 redirect to the attacker-controlled external URL. This enables phishing attacks where a user, believing they are still on the legitimate MISP Modules site, may enter additional credentials or sensitive information on the attacker's page. It can also be used to obscure the true destination of a link, bypassing user trust in the legitimate domain. The vulnerability requires the victim to interact with the crafted URL and complete a login, but no prior authentication or special configuration is needed on the attacker's side. The affected component is the website sub-project of misp-modules, specifically the account blueprint in website/app/account/account.py. No version boundaries are specified in the patch metadata.
CVE-2026-128637.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-59074.title: Improper Cryptographic Signature Verification in Edito CMS
CVE-2026-59074.desc:
Edito CMS is vulnerable to improper cryptographic signature verification in the JWT refresh logic. An authenticated low-privilege user can submit self-crafted​ ​JWT​ containing​ ​an existing user​ ​identifier and, due to the lack of signature validation,​​  obtain​ ​a ​​valid,​​ fully-signed​​ session ​​token​​ for​​ any ​​account ​​in​ ​the​ ​system. This allows the attacker to impersonate any user, including administrators.
This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

When an administrator visits the admin changelog logs, the injected script is automatically executed, in his browser.

CVE-2026-116615.desc: The Widget Options – Advanced Conditional Visibility for Gutenberg Blocks & Classic Widgets plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Code Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.6.1 via the `post_content` parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to inject PHP expressions that execute on every front-end page view, enabling boolean-oracle exfiltration of WordPress site configuration data — including admin email address, default role, and arbitrary `get_option`, `get_user_meta`, and `get_post_meta` values — via the plugin's allowlisted-function sandbox, which escalates to unrestricted code execution if any installed plugin extends the `widgetopts_allowed_php_functions` filter. Contributors can also exploit this vulnerability when their submitted post is later published by an administrator; notably, the injected payload executes for all site visitors, including unauthenticated users, because a trust-flag mechanism introduced in version 4.2.6 causes `widgetopts_safe_eval_trusted()` to bypass its non-admin short-circuit at every legacy render callsite. Exploitation by attackers with contributor-level access and above requires that an administrator (or editor) later publishes the contributor's submission. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

CVE-2026-126278.desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains a race condition vulnerability in users.service.ts that allows holders of a valid reset token to perform multiple password changes by sending concurrent reset requests. CVE-2026-126278.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126279.desc: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in PromptWithFields.vue that renders unescaped field references from AI field prompts as HTML in a tooltip. Attackers with the Creator role or above can store markup in a prompt's field reference that executes when victims open the field configuration, stealing the localStorage session token to call authenticated APIs as the victim.
CVE-2026-126279.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126280.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Refresh Token Reuse via Non-Atomic Rotation
CVE-2026-126280.desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a race condition in refresh-token rotation that allows attackers to reuse tokens because UserRefreshToken.ts never checks the affected-row count. Attackers holding a captured refresh token can present it concurrently with the legitimate user to obtain a valid authenticated session, and no reuse event is recorded.
CVE-2026-126280.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126281.desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the copy-from branch of integration creation in integrations.service.ts that decrypts a source integration's connection credentials without checking its owner or private flag. Authenticated users with the Creator role can supply guessed or enumerated integration ids to copy other users' private database host, username, and password into an integration they own.
CVE-2026-126281.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126282.title: NocoDB from 2026.04.0 before 2026.08.0 Improper Privilege Management via Organization Role Update
CVE-2026-126282.desc: NocoDB from 2026.04.0 before 2026.08.0 contains an improper privilege management vulnerability in org-users.service.ts where updating a user's legacy organization role rewrites their default-workspace role. Revoked users can silently regain Creator-level read, write and schema modification access across all default-workspace bases using their existing session token.
CVE-2026-126282.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126283.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Incorrect Authorization via Base-Scoped API Tokens
CVE-2026-126283.desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that lets base-scoped API tokens act as account-wide credentials because the token's base_id is never stored or checked. Attackers holding a leaked token can read, write and delete records on every base the token owner belongs to, including bases joined later.
CVE-2026-126283.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126284.desc: NocoDB from 2026.05.2 before 2026.07.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Editor-role users to fetch internal URLs because data import reused the webhook internal-network exemption. When NC_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOOKS or NC_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK is set, attackers can request internal services via URLs ending in CSV or spreadsheet extensions and read the responses.
CVE-2026-126284.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126285.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 SQL Injection via Legacy where Query Filter
CVE-2026-126285.desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with read access to run arbitrary read queries via the legacy where parameter on PostgreSQL. Attackers, including Viewer-role users, can inject single quotes into filter values concatenated by CustomKnex.ts to read other tables, schemas, view-filtered rows, and hidden columns.
CVE-2026-126285.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126286.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Reflected XSS via ncRedirectUrl in PageLeavingWarning.vue
CVE-2026-126286.desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in PageLeavingWarning.vue that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute script by embedding an ASCII control character in the ncRedirectUrl scheme. Attackers can send a crafted link that bypasses the scheme check and reaches the anchor href or window.location, stealing the session token from localStorage for account takeover.
CVE-2026-126286.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126287.desc: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains a race condition vulnerability in oauth-token.service.ts that allows attackers to reuse a refresh token by presenting it concurrently during non-atomic rotation. Attackers holding a captured refresh token can race the legitimate client to obtain their own access and refresh tokens, retaining scoped access without triggering reuse detection.
CVE-2026-126287.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126288.desc: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve full OAuth client records by querying the public client lookup route in oauth.controller.ts. Attackers who know or guess a client identifier can obtain the registration access token to modify or delete registrations, plus the bcrypt client secret hash and owner's internal identifier.
CVE-2026-126288.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126289.desc: NocoDB before 2026.06.1 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability in export.service.ts that writes record values and column titles beginning with formula characters into CSV exports without neutralization. Low-privileged collaborators, or unauthenticated users submitting a public form, can plant formulas that execute when a user opens the export in a spreadsheet application, potentially exfiltrating cell contents or invoking external commands.
CVE-2026-126289.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126290.desc: NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in base-integrations.service.ts that allows authenticated base members to read private integration configurations by omitting a query flag. Attackers can request another user's private integration without the configuration flag, bypassing the ownership check to obtain stored connection credentials.
CVE-2026-126290.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126291.title: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 SQL Injection via User Email in Base User Query
CVE-2026-126291.desc: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in base-user.cte.utils.ts, which concatenates base members' email addresses into the SQL text of queries resolving user, created-by or last-modified-by fields. Registered users can set an email with a quoted local part containing a single quote to execute arbitrary SQL, exposing user records, API tokens and data-source credentials.
CVE-2026-126291.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126292.desc: NocoDB before 2026.06.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the profile update handler in users.service.ts, which returns the stored user record without passing it through the user-serialization filter, exposing the bcrypt password hash, salt, and session token counter. Attackers holding a stolen or hijacked session can update the profile to retrieve that account's password hash and salt for offline cracking.
CVE-2026-126292.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126293.desc: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains an attachment size limit bypass that allows authenticated Editor users to store oversized files because data-attachment-v3.service.ts trusts the remote server's advertised content length. Attackers can point the v3 upload-by-URL endpoint at a server that understates or omits its length to exhaust disk space or storage quota.
CVE-2026-126293.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126294.title: Grav Login Plugin before 3.11.0 Two-Factor Authentication Bypass via /login
CVE-2026-126294.desc: Grav Login plugin before 3.11.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers with an account password to skip two-factor verification when the global twofa_enabled setting is off. Attackers can sign in through the /login form, remember-me cookie, or magic link to obtain a session the API plugin accepts, gaining full account permissions including super-admin control.
CVE-2026-126294.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126295.desc: NLTK from 3.10.0 before 3.10.4 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability in BllipParser that allows attackers to open files outside NLTK data roots by supplying unvalidated model paths. Attackers controlling parser_model, reranker_features, reranker_weights, or from_unified_model_dir() input can make the bllipparser C extension read sensitive files or block on FIFOs and devices.
CVE-2026-126295.path: local access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126296.desc: NLTK before 3.10.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in save_maxent_params() and load_maxent_params() that bypasses the pathsec filesystem restriction mechanism. Attackers who control the tab_dir argument can read or overwrite model parameter files outside permitted data roots, because the functions call Python's built-in open() directly.
CVE-2026-126296.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126300.desc: NLTK from 3.2.5 before 3.10.4 contains an algorithmic complexity vulnerability in TreebankWordTokenizer.span_tokenize that allows remote attackers to cause quadratic CPU consumption through repeated list.pop(0) calls. Attackers can submit long runs of double-quote characters to services span-tokenizing untrusted text, exhausting a CPU core and degrading availability.
CVE-2026-126300.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126301.desc: NLTK from 3.6 before 3.10.4 contains an algorithmic complexity vulnerability in LegalitySyllableTokenizer.tokenize that allows remote attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying long all-vowel tokens. Attackers can submit a token such as a long run of vowels, causing the unguarded onset reversal loop to perform quadratic work and deny service to syllabification components.
CVE-2026-126301.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126302.desc: NLTK from 3.9.4 before 3.10.4 contains a symlink following vulnerability in nltk.sem.chat80.sql_query() that bypasses the pathsec data-root sandbox containment check. Attackers who can write into a trusted NLTK data root can plant a symbolic link to read SQLite databases outside the sandbox.
CVE-2026-126302.path: local access needed, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126305.title: EspoCRM before 10.0.9 Stored XSS via Knowledge Base Article Attachments
CVE-2026-126305.desc: EspoCRM before 9.3.11 and 10.x before 10.0.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Knowledge Base articles that lets users with Knowledge Base create or edit access attach a JavaScript file and add a crafted link to the article body. When an administrator clicks the link, the script runs in their session and can create an administrator account with attacker-chosen credentials.
CVE-2026-126305.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126306.title: EspoCRM before 10.0.8 Stored XSS via Malicious SVG Attachment
CVE-2026-126306.desc: EspoCRM before 9.3.11 and 10.x before 10.0.8 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged users to upload crafted SVG images that submit authenticated POST requests to arbitrary backend endpoints. Attackers can trick an administrator into opening the SVG in a separate browser tab and clicking it, performing administrator actions such as elevating the attacker's account to administrator.
CVE-2026-126306.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126307.title: Nezha Dashboard before 2.6.0 Multiple Authorization and Tenant Isolation Flaws
CVE-2026-126307.desc: Nezha Dashboard before 2.6.0 contains multiple authorization, tenant isolation, and resource exhaustion vulnerabilities that allow members or unauthenticated attackers to abuse NAT, DDNS, OAuth, cron, and server transfer features. Attackers can claim undeclared Dashboard hostnames to capture login bodies, hijack DDNS profiles, create executable schedules without exec scope, or exhaust memory via buffered NAT requests.
CVE-2026-126307.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126308.title: Coder 2.38.0 before 2.38.2 Session Token Leak via Sub-Agent External Apps
CVE-2026-126308.desc: The web dashboard in Coder 2.24.0 before 2.29.23, 2.30.0 before 2.34.14, 2.35.0 before 2.36.9, 2.37.0 before 2.37.6, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.2 replaces the $SESSION_TOKEN placeholder in external app URLs with a full-access API key without checking whether the app belongs to a sub-agent. Code running in a workspace can register a disguised sub-agent app with a custom protocol URL, so the owner's click sends their API key to an attacker-chosen destination.
CVE-2026-126308.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126309.title: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 Path Traversal in Transit Key Import
CVE-2026-126309.desc: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in Transit key import that allows authenticated attackers to bypass name restrictions in ACL policies. Attackers limited by a required_parameters name constraint can craft traversal sequences during import to write key material under arbitrary Transit key names.
CVE-2026-126309.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126310.title: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 OIDC Provider Authentication Bypass via Client Credentials
CVE-2026-126310.desc: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated callers to obtain OIDC ID tokens by abusing public clients with client_credentials enabled. Attackers who know a public client's client_id can request tokens from the identity/oidc/provider/<name>/token endpoint to impersonate the client without any secret.
CVE-2026-126310.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126311.desc: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.x before 2.7.2 does not neutralize wildcard characters in SSH certificate principals rendered from unvalidated external token metadata via identity templates in the SSH secrets engine. Attackers controlling that metadata, typically through a compromised identity provider, can inject '*' to obtain SSH certificates valid for multiple hosts or users.
CVE-2026-126311.path: remote, needs admin rights, no user action

CVE-2026-126312.title: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 ACL Bypass via Non-Canonical Plugin Paths
CVE-2026-126312.desc: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.x before 2.7.2, and the openbao-plugins LDAP and RADIUS auth plugins before 0.2.0, contain an ACL bypass in the AppRole, Cert, LDAP, and RADIUS auth methods caused by implicit path canonicalization. Authenticated attackers can request non-canonical paths for AppRole Role IDs, Cert CRLs, LDAP groups and users, or RADIUS users to evade ACL deny rules.
CVE-2026-126312.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126313.desc: Frappe HRMS 16.0.0 before 16.20.1 contains an authorization bypass because an ownership check is missing on a record type that employees can create. Authenticated users holding only the Employee role can create or change draft records for another employee, or for a company they do not belong to.
CVE-2026-126313.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126314.title: Frappe HRMS 15.0.0 before 15.64.6 Missing Authorization in Bulk Record Creation
CVE-2026-126314.desc: Frappe HRMS 15.0.0 before 15.64.6 and 16.0.0 before 16.20.1 does not check access to each employee on endpoints that create records in bulk for a list of employees. An authenticated user with create permission on the affected record type, such as HR User, can create records for employees outside their user-permission scope, including other companies' employees.
CVE-2026-126314.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126315.title: Frappe HRMS 16.14.0 before 16.20.1 Telemetry Setting Bypass Information Exposure
CVE-2026-126315.desc: Frappe HRMS 16.14.0 before 16.20.1 sends product usage events on certain HR transactions without checking the site's telemetry setting, and some events include more detail than needed. During normal use, with no user action, values such as leave type names, claimed amounts and appraisal scores are transmitted even when telemetry is disabled.
CVE-2026-126315.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126316.desc: Frappe HRMS from 16.0.0 before 16.20.1 contains an information exposure vulnerability that places the subscription key in the query string of outbound subscription status requests. Attackers with access to proxy, server, or monitoring logs along the request path can recover the site's subscription key from recorded URLs.
CVE-2026-126316.path: remote, needs admin rights, no user action

CVE-2026-126317.title: Frappe HRMS 16.0.0 before 16.20.1 Missing Authorization in Company Details Endpoint
CVE-2026-126317.desc: Frappe HRMS from 16.0.0 before 16.20.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read company details outside their permissions due to a missing permission check. Any logged-in user, including Employee role users, can query the affected endpoint to list every company on the site along with its default currency.
CVE-2026-126317.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126318.desc: REDAXO before 5.21.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows editors without the version[live_version] permission to modify live article versions by bypassing working version enforcement. Authenticated editors can add, edit, delete, toggle, or reorder live slices via content/functions, slice ids, content_slice_status, content_move_slice, history restore, or content_copy, bypassing approval workflows.
CVE-2026-126318.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126319.desc: Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows authenticated users with stacks:create permission to read sensitive files by supplying an arbitrary composePath during stack adoption. Attackers can adopt a stack pointing to the encryption key, SQLite database, or /proc/self/environ and read it via the compose endpoint to obtain all stored credentials.
CVE-2026-126319.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126320.desc: Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that lets users holding only containers:view download arbitrary container files instead of requiring containers:exec. Authenticated Enterprise RBAC users can request any path from the files/download endpoint, which reads through Docker's archive API, to retrieve secrets, keys, and mounted credentials.
CVE-2026-126320.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126321.title: Dockhand before 1.0.55 Path Traversal via Symlink in File-Browser Endpoints
CVE-2026-126321.desc: Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users with stacks:edit to bypass the file-browser path guard by combining symlinks with '..' sequences. Attackers can read /proc/self/environ, the SQLite database, and the encryption key via /api/system/files/content, or move them using the stack relocate endpoint, exposing stored credentials.
CVE-2026-126321.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126322.title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Unsanitized Deserialization via patient_match_dialog.php
CVE-2026-126322.desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an unsanitized deserialization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to control patient-matching criteria by supplying a crafted serialized key parameter. Attackers can send serialized arrays to interface/orders/patient_match_dialog.php to enumerate patients or force matches that associate lab orders with the wrong patient.
CVE-2026-126322.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126323.desc: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to perform admin state-changing actions because checkCsrf() in admin/controller/base.php only validates tokens for POST requests. Attackers can lure a logged-in admin into loading a forged cross-site GET request to delete admin/user accounts, sites, orders, and menus or change comment status.
CVE-2026-126323.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126369.desc: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privilege author or vendor users to inject script by bypassing the regex blacklist in sanitizeHTML(). Attackers can save post or product content with unclosed event-handler tags or javascript: entities to execute script for anonymous visitors and admins, enabling session or CSRF-token theft.
CVE-2026-126369.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-126370.title: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 Authenticated RCE via .sql Code Injection in editor/code/save
CVE-2026-126370.desc: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains a remote code execution vulnerability allowing restricted site_admin roles to inject PHP by saving .sql files through the admin code editor. Attackers can bypass extension and content deny-lists with an @IF macro payload that compiles into executable PHP when the model loads, running OS commands as the web user.
CVE-2026-126370.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126371.desc: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in Admin_Auth_TokenSQL::update(), which interpolates admin_auth_token array keys into an INSERT column list without a column whitelist or backtick escaping. Authenticated admin-panel users can submit backtick-containing keys to the admin/auth-token save action to inject comments and column identifiers into the SQL statement.
CVE-2026-126371.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126372.title: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 Template Upload Bypass via MediaTrait editor/code
CVE-2026-126372.desc: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-41934 that allows authenticated editor or site_admin users to write server-side templates by bypassing save restrictions. Attackers can upload or rename .tpl files via editor/code upload and rename actions, or evade isExecutableFile checks in save(), to inject PHP code into templates.
CVE-2026-126372.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126373.desc: Vvveb 1.0.8.4 through 1.0.8.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the content/revisions revision action that lets low-privileged Authors read other authors' revisions. Attackers can supply a post_id, language_id, and created_at timestamp to retrieve private unpublished drafts, because the revision() action lacks the admin_id ownership restriction.
CVE-2026-126373.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126374.desc: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because the @KEYS(:each) macro emits PHP array keys as backtick-quoted INSERT column names without escaping, and several procedures in admin/sql/mysqli/product.sql and admin_auth_token.sql omit the @FILTER guard. Authenticated back-office users able to save products can submit product_<feature> POST array keys containing backticks to redirect bound values into unexposed columns or break SQL statements.
CVE-2026-126374.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126375.title: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 Cross-Tenant Digital Asset Tampering via Media Trait
CVE-2026-126375.desc: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows low-privilege vendors to rename, delete, or overwrite other vendors' digital-asset files in the shared storage/digital_assets directory. Attackers can send rename, delete, or upload requests to product/digital-asset with another vendor's filename to break downloads or substitute malicious content.
CVE-2026-126375.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126376.desc: Vvveb 1.0.8.4 through 1.0.8.6 contains an incomplete authorization fix that allows low-privilege authors and vendors to access other users' records by bypassing admin_id owner scoping. Attackers can supply filter[admin_id] to list drafts, invoke duplicate() on posts or products, or enumerate every vendor's digital-asset metadata.
CVE-2026-126376.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126377.title: Vvveb before 1.0.9.0 Cookie Forgery via PHP Type Juggling in generateCookie()
CVE-2026-126377.desc: Vvveb before 1.0.9.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in generateCookie() in system/user/user.php that uses loose comparison to validate MD5 cookie hashes. Unauthenticated attackers can brute-force cookie values until the server's MD5 computation yields a 0e magic hash, then forge persistent cookies for account takeover.
CVE-2026-126377.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126378.title: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 Webshell Upload via Theme Installer validFile() Bypass
CVE-2026-126378.desc: Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains a file upload vulnerability in the theme installer validFile() function that uses strpos() instead of strict path matching. Attackers with admin credentials can upload a ZIP containing a PHP file whose path includes /theme.php to achieve remote code execution on nginx deployments.
CVE-2026-126378.path: remote, needs admin rights, no user action

CVE-2026-126379.title: Vvveb 1.0.8.6 SSRF via oEmbed Proxy DNS Rebinding
CVE-2026-126379.desc: Vvveb 1.0.8.6 contains an incomplete server-side request forgery fix that allows authenticated admin users to bypass DNS pinning by requesting non-443 URLs. Attackers can supply a rebinding hostname to the editor oEmbedProxy url parameter to read loopback services, internal panels, and cloud metadata credentials.
CVE-2026-126379.path: remote, needs admin rights, no user action

CVE-2026-126380.title: Vvveb before 1.0.9.0 RCE via .phar Extension Denylist Bypass in Media Upload
CVE-2026-126380.desc: Vvveb before 1.0.9.0 contains a denylist bypass in system/traits/media.php where '.phar' is misconfigured with a leading dot, allowing authenticated administrators to upload .phar PHP files. Attackers can upload a GIF magic-byte polyglot webshell bypassing binary inspection and execute arbitrary OS commands as the web-server user.
CVE-2026-126380.path: remote, needs admin rights, no user action

CVE-2026-126381.desc: n8n before 2.43.5, 2.44.x before 2.44.1, and 3.x before 3.0.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the Vector Store (OracleDB) node, which does not validate Metadata Filter keys used in vector search queries. Attackers can supply crafted filter keys through untrusted workflow input such as webhooks to read data accessible to the configured Oracle credential.
CVE-2026-126381.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126382.desc: n8n before 2.38.0 and 3.x before 3.0.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the Asana Trigger that accepts a new webhook verification secret from any request carrying an X-Hook-Secret header. Unauthenticated attackers who know the webhook URL can replace the secret, send forged Asana events that pass signature verification, and trigger workflows with attacker-controlled data while genuine deliveries are rejected.
CVE-2026-126382.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-126383.title: n8n before 1.123.89 NoSQL Injection via MongoDB Node Update Key
CVE-2026-126383.desc: n8n before 1.123.89, 2.x before 2.45.5, 2.46.x before 2.46.1, and 3.x before 3.0.1 contains a NoSQL injection vulnerability in the MongoDB node's Update and Find And Replace operations due to insufficient validation of the update key value taken from incoming items. Attackers who can supply untrusted input, such as a webhook body, to a workflow using these operations can make the node match and overwrite unintended documents or insert new documents in the MongoDB database.
CVE-2026-126383.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126384.title: n8n before 1.123.89 RCE via Bundled GraphicsMagick in Edit Image Node
CVE-2026-126384.desc: n8n before 1.123.89, 2.x before 2.45.5, 2.46.x before 2.46.1, and 3.x before 3.0.1 bundles a GraphicsMagick version with known vulnerabilities in its official Docker image, which the Edit Image node uses to process images. Attackers who can supply crafted untrusted images to an Edit Image workflow, such as one fed by a Webhook node, can execute code on the n8n instance.
CVE-2026-126384.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-126385.title: n8n before 2.46.1 OAuth Account Hijack via Unauthenticated Credential Callback
CVE-2026-126385.desc: n8n before 2.45.5, 2.46.x before 2.46.1, and 3.x before 3.0.1 contains a flaw in the OAuth2 credential callback of the dynamic-credential connect flow, which does not verify that the completing browser belongs to the user who started the flow. Members with access to a resolvable OAuth2 credential can send the provider authorization URL to a victim; if the victim consents without an active n8n session, the victim's tokens are stored under the member's identity, letting the member's workflows act as the victim.
CVE-2026-126385.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-120221.title: frr: bgpd double free of peer-group Site-of-Origin when dynamic neighbors disconnect
CVE-2026-120221.desc: In FRRouting, bgpd frees the same memory twice when dynamic BGP neighbors disconnect, if the peer-group used by a "bgp listen range" also has a Site-of-Origin configured ("neighbor PG soo"). Each dynamic neighbor shares the peer-group's SoO value instead of getting its own copy, but frees it as its own when the neighbor is deleted, which happens as soon as its connection closes. The first disconnect leaves the peer-group pointing at freed memory, and the second disconnect frees it again, causing bgpd to abort and drop all BGP sessions on the router. Any host whose address falls inside the listen range can trigger this by opening and closing two TCP connections to the BGP port, without sending any BGP message and without knowing the AS number, and can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. If the peer-group has a TCP-MD5 password, only hosts that know the password can trigger it. Two ordinary flaps of legitimate dynamic neighbors have the same effect. Between the two frees, displaying the configuration ("show running-config") or establishing a dynamic neighbor also reads the freed memory, which can crash bgpd after a single disconnect. Only configurations that combine a listen range with a SoO on the same peer-group are affected.
CVE-2026-120221.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124758.desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user record index against the size of the record block header. The 32-bit length is reduced by the header size before it is passed to the record handlers, so a length smaller than the header underflows and the handlers receive a data length of about 65530. The fixed-size reads of the I&M and PDPort handlers can then read past the end of the session buffer. The result of the write is discarded. The attacker must have an established Application Relationship or be able to send in the context of one, and requires ADJACENT network access.
CVE-2026-124758.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124759.title: Alarm frames are accepted from any source address

A host with ADJACENT network access can abort an established Application Relationship with a single alarm ERROR frame, or deliver forged alarm notifications with chosen type, slot, subslot, USI and payload to the application.
CVE-2026-124759.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124760.desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 sets the alarm receiver state to waiting for confirmation before the data of a received alarm notification is parsed. If the parsing fails the state is not restored, and later alarm notifications of the same priority are discarded without acknowledge until the Application Relationship is released. The Application Relationship and the cyclic data exchange keep working. The attacker must be able to send an alarm notification in the context of an established Application Relationship and requires ADJACENT network access.
CVE-2026-124760.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124761.title: A DCP Set of the IP suite that is refused is still stored

If the request is refused, for example because an Application Relationship is active, the configuration is not restored and is still saved. After a restart the device uses the refused address, and may not answer the controller or may use its address. A host with ADJACENT network access can use this while an Application Relationship is active.
CVE-2026-124761.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124762.desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 finds the RPC session of a received PDU by its activity UUID only, and a reject, fault or cancel PDU for the session aborts the Application Relationship, without checking that the PDU is the answer to a call of the device or where it comes from. A host with ADJACENT network access that has observed the activity UUID of the connection, which is sent in clear in every RPC request, can abort the Application Relationship with one PDU. It also allocates a session for an unknown activity UUID and changes the address stored for an existing session.
CVE-2026-124762.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-127122.title: Out-of-bounds write with too many MCR blocks in a Connect request

Each further block is written past the end of the array, into the rest of the Application Relationship and, with more blocks, into the following one. The written data comes from the request. No established Application Relationship is needed, and the attacker requires ADJACENT network access. Builds with PNET_OPTION_MC_CR disabled are not affected.

CVE-2026-127123.desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 releases the Application Relationship of an RPC session, without the abort procedure, when a fragment of a request has another data representation (endianness) than the first fragment of the call. The application is not told that the Application Relationship is gone, the cyclic data stops, and the resources of the Application Relationship are left referencing a cleared structure. Another host can then connect in its place. A host with ADJACENT network access that has observed the activity UUID of the connection, which is sent in clear in every RPC request, can do this with one PDU.
CVE-2026-127123.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-127124.title: RPC session pool exhausted by unfinished fragmented requests
CVE-2026-127124.desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 keeps the RPC session that is allocated for a fragment of a request with an unknown activity UUID, without a timeout, when the rest of the request never arrives. A session that does not get an Application Relationship is also kept after the response. Repeated fragments or requests with different activity UUIDs exhaust the available sessions, one UDP packet per session. Once they are exhausted the device no longer answers a Connect request until it is restarted. An unauthenticated attacker with ADJACENT network access can use this to cause a denial of service.
CVE-2026-127124.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-127125.desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 aborts the Application Relationship of an RPC session when a fragment of a response has been resent without being acknowledged, without checking that the session has an Application Relationship. A request for an existing Application Relationship that is sent on another activity than its Connect, and gets a fragmented response, is handled on a session without one. If the response is not acknowledged, a NULL pointer is dereferenced and the device crashes. A conformant IO-controller does not send such requests. The attacker must have observed the AR UUID of an established Application Relationship and requires ADJACENT network access.
CVE-2026-127125.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-128790.desc:
In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment do not apply an access rule's `FILTERLIST` fragment filters to single Submodel reads.



`GET /submodels` removes the fields that a rule's `FILTERLIST` hides, but `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}` and `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$metadata` return them unfiltered. An authenticated caller with READ access to a Submodel can therefore read fields that the access rules hide from them, for example `supplementalSemanticIds` keys that name the other parties allowed to read the Submodel.



If versioning is enabled (`history.mode` set to `api` or `audit`), `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$history` and `GET /shells/{aasIdentifier}/$history` in the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment return the complete stored version without applying the rule's formula or fragment filters. A caller whose rules grant READ on these routes can read fields that the access rules hide, and Submodels and Asset Administration Shells that the direct read does not return to them at all.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.
CVE-2026-128790.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action
