CVE-2026-93666.desc:
The Bluetooth Classic SDP client built its outgoing request PDUs with bt_sdp_create_pdu(), which allocates from the sdp_pool net-buf pool with a K_FOREVER timeout and no failure handling, in sdp_client_ss_search(), sdp_client_sa_search() and sdp_client_ssa_search() in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/sdp.c. All of these run on the Bluetooth workqueue bt_workq (via sdp_client_work_handler(), the L2CAP sdp_client_connected() callback, or the continuation-state follow-up from a received response), which is the same single thread that dispatches incoming HCI ACL and event traffic, drives L2CAP, and performs connection and channel teardown. sdp_pool holds only CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN buffers (one by default) and is shared with the SDP server role.

An unauthenticated peer within BR/EDR range can drive both halves of the trigger. The SDP L2CAP server is registered at BT_SECURITY_L0, so any inbound SDP request makes the device allocate the pool's buffer for a response, which is held until the controller has transmitted it. The same peer can then cause a client request to be issued while the pool is empty: in-tree profiles start SDP discovery from inbound connection callbacks (for example hfp_hf_accept() calls bt_sdp_discover() through hfp_hf_create(), and hfp_ag.c mirrors this), and a peer acting as an SDP server can force repeated client requests by answering with partial responses carrying continuation state.

With the pool empty, the allocation blocks uninterruptibly and freezes the entire Bluetooth host. The stall becomes permanent when the release of the outstanding buffer itself depends on the blocked workqueue: if the link carrying the queued PDU is dropped or stalls, hci_disconn_complete() and the L2CAP channel cleanup that purges the channel TX queue are themselves bt_workq work items, so the buffer is never returned. The result is an unrecoverable denial of service of all Bluetooth functionality until reboot; there is no memory-safety, confidentiality or integrity impact.

The fix allocates client PDUs with K_NO_WAIT via a new sdp_client_create_pdu(), propagates -ENOBUFS, parks the session on a new SDP_CLIENT_FLAG_WAIT_FOR_TX_BUF flag, and adds an sdp_pool destructor that re-submits the SDP client worker when a buffer becomes available. Note that the SDP server role still allocated from the same pool with K_FOREVER at this commit; that path was addressed separately.
CVE-2026-93666.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-93667.desc:
The Virtual L2 receive handler virtual_recv() in subsys/net/l2/virtual/virtual.c ends with a fall-through path meant for a virtual interface that has nothing attached below it: it takes net_if_get_device(iface)->api, treats it as a struct virtual_interface_api, and calls api->recv(iface, pkt). That handler is however also invoked with a non-virtual interface: ethernet_recv() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c deliberately passes the Ethernet interface so that a tagged frame can be dispatched over the VLAN interfaces attached to it. For an Ethernet interface dev->api is a struct ethernet_api, whose layout only shares the leading struct net_if_api, so the slot read as recv is actually get_config() (default) or get_capabilities() (when CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS_ETHERNET is enabled).

The fall-through is reached whenever no attached virtual interface claims the frame - most simply when the VLAN interface owning the frame's tag exists but is administratively down, since net_eth_get_vlan_iface() resolves the tag without checking link state while virtual_recv() skips interfaces that are not up. Any host able to place an 802.1Q-tagged Ethernet frame on the same link can then trigger the mistyped indirect call; no authentication, IP reachability or user interaction is required, because the frame is consumed at L2 before any address check.

The resulting call passes a struct net_if  where the driver expects a struct device  and a struct net_pkt  where it expects a struct net_if , with the callee's remaining parameters left as whatever the call site happens to leave in the argument registers. Driver implementations dereference these values: get_capabilities() typically reads dev->config/dev->data (a wild read through a non-pointer field of struct net_if), and get_config() implementations write through the uninitialized struct ethernet_config * argument. The practical impact is undefined behaviour in the network RX path - crashes and uncontrolled memory corruption - plus mis-handling of the packet when a capability bitmask is returned as a net_verdict. The attacker controls neither the corrupted address nor the value written, so this is a denial-of-service and memory-corruption issue rather than a controllable write primitive.

The same defective fall-through is reachable through any_recv() in subsys/net/l2/dummy/any/any.c, which passes a dummy interface whose struct dummy_api is shorter than the offset read, producing an out-of-bounds read of the driver's API object followed by an indirect call. The fix drops any packet whose interface is not a Virtual L2 interface, closing both entry points.
CVE-2026-93667.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-93668.desc:
The Bluetooth Classic SDP server in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/sdp.c allocated every response PDU through bt_sdp_create_pdu(), which expands to bt_l2cap_create_pdu() and therefore uses a K_FOREVER timeout. The allocation is made from sdp_pool, a fixed pool holding only CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN buffers (one in the default configuration) that is shared with the SDP client role. When the pool is empty the call blocks without a bound.

The allocation is reached from bt_sdp_recv() on the Bluetooth host's RX context: the bt_workq "BT RX WQ" workqueue in the default configuration since v3.1.0, and the dedicated "BT RX" thread before that. This context processes all normal-priority HCI events and all received ACL data. The SDP L2CAP server is registered on PSM 0x0001 with no security requirement (BT_SECURITY_L0), so an unpaired, unauthenticated BR/EDR peer within radio range of a connectable device can drive it. Every malformed or unrecognised SDP PDU reaches send_err_rsp(), and the sdp_svc_search_req(), sdp_svc_att_req() and sdp_svc_search_att_req() handlers allocate as well, so a short burst of pipelined requests drains the pool and parks the RX context in the blocking allocation.

A pool buffer is released only once its response has been sent, and a peer that withholds baseband acknowledgements keeps the controller's buffers for the link full, so the response is never sent. While the RX context is blocked, the entire Bluetooth host, for all connections and both LE and BR/EDR, stops processing normal-priority HCI events and received data. In most affected releases the stall is permanent. Queued PDUs are freed only by connection or channel teardown, which waits for the normal-priority Disconnection Complete handler, and that handler runs on the blocked RX context, so the host does not recover without a reset. In v3.7.0 through v4.1.x the TX processor discards the queued response once the link supervision timeout drops the connection, so each stall ends at that timeout, but the peer can reconnect and repeat it for as long as it stays in range. The impact is limited to availability; no memory corruption or information disclosure is involved.

The fix adds sdp_svc_create_pdu() using K_NO_WAIT, pre-allocates the response buffer once in bt_sdp_recv(), stashes the request in sdp->recv_pending when no buffer is available, and retries it from a work handler once a buffer is freed by the pool destroy callback.
CVE-2026-93668.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-93669.desc:
The ITE IT8xxx2 SHI host-command backend in subsys/mgmt/ec_host_cmd/backends/ec_host_cmd_backend_shi_ite.c arms the SPI peripheral before its receive context exists. shi_ite_init_registers() sets the state machine to SHI_STATE_READY_TO_RECV and calls irq_enable() while the device initializes at POST_KERNEL priority CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT (40), but data->rx_ctx and data->tx are only assigned later by shi_ite_backend_init(), which ec_host_cmd_init() invokes at CONFIG_EC_HOST_CMD_INIT_PRIORITY (default 80).

If the attached host processor starts a SPI transaction inside that window, the Rx-valid-length interrupt fires, shi_ite_int_handler() passes its state check and calls shi_ite_parse_header(), which stores the host-derived request length through the still-NULL data->rx_ctx. On the IT8xxx2 low addresses are not backed by RAM, and with CONFIG_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION_DETECTION_PMP the first bytes of the address space are explicitly made inaccessible, so the store raises a fatal access fault in interrupt context. The window widens further when CONFIG_EC_HOST_CMD_INITIALIZE_AT_BOOT is disabled and the application calls ec_host_cmd_init() itself.

The result is a kernel panic on the embedded controller: with Zephyr's default fatal handler the CPU halts, so the controller stops servicing host commands until a hardware reset. Because the trigger is traffic from the attached host processor -- an untrusted peer from the controller firmware's point of view -- software on that host can provoke the fault by forcing a controller reset and issuing transactions during the reboot, turning a recoverable reset into a persistent outage. Impact is limited to availability: the faulting address is fixed and not attacker-chosen, so no memory-corruption primitive follows.

The fix leaves the interface at SHI_STATE_DISABLED with the interrupt masked during device init, moves irq_enable() into shi_ite_backend_init() after the buffers are published, and makes shi_ite_int_handler() reject a NULL data->rx_ctx while write-clearing IT83XX_SPI_ISR and IT83XX_SPI_RX_VLISR so that an unexpected early interrupt cannot storm.
CVE-2026-93669.path: local access needed, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-93670.desc:
The Synopsys DesignWare I3C controller driver (drivers/i3c/i3c_dw.c) tracks free Device Address Table (DAT) slots with get_free_pos(), which signals an exhausted table by returning -1. The helper declared its return type as uint8_t, so the sentinel was truncated to 255, and both consumers (dw_i3c_attach_device() and dw_i3c_i2c_attach_device()) also stored it in a uint8_t before testing if (pos < 0) — a comparison that is never true for an unsigned value. The exhaustion guard was therefore inert in every build.

With the guard defeated, an attach attempted on a full DAT proceeds with pos == 255: it writes data->dw_i3c_i2c_priv_data[255].id, more than 200 bytes past the end of the 32-element dw_i3c_i2c_priv_data array and past the end of struct dw_i3c_data; it stores the resulting out-of-bounds address in desc->controller_priv, from which later detach, reattach and IBI operations read the slot index back; and it performs a 32-bit MMIO store 1020 bytes beyond the hardware DAT base, outside the table the controller reports. The attach still returns success, so the upper layer believes the device is bound.

The DAT is smaller than the software array (its depth is read from DEVICE_ADDR_TABLE_POINTER, commonly 8 or 16 entries), so exhaustion is reachable. In a dual-role build (CONFIG_I3C_DUAL_ROLE with CONFIG_I3C_USE_IBI) acting as a secondary controller, the attach count is supplied by the bus's active controller: i3c_sec_handoffed() attaches one device per entry of the received DEFTGTS list, so a hostile or malfunctioning controller on the local I3C bus that declares more targets than the local DAT depth triggers the condition once per surplus entry. Exhaustion can also be reached from a devicetree that declares more devices than the table holds, or by repeated i3c attach shell commands.

Impact is bounded: the out-of-bounds store is a single byte of fixed value at a fixed displacement, with no attacker-chosen data or offset, so the realistic outcomes are corruption of neighbouring static driver state, writes into reserved controller registers, and inconsistent driver bookkeeping (a crash or a wedged I3C bus) rather than a controllable memory-write primitive. The attack vector is the local chip-to-chip I3C bus; there is no network-reachable path.
CVE-2026-93670.path: physical access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-93671.desc:
The websocket client's HTTP header callback on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c receives the Sec-WebSocket-Accept header value as a pointer/length pair from the HTTP parser. The referenced bytes live inside the application-supplied receive buffer and are not NUL terminated. When the received value did not match the expected accept key, the pointer was passed directly to a %s conversion in a NET_DBG() call, so the logging code measured the string with strlen() and read on past the end of the header value looking for a terminator.

The value is supplied by the peer during the WebSocket handshake, before any application-level authentication, so a malicious or man-in-the-middle server reached over a ws:// (or otherwise attacker-terminated) connection can trigger the mismatch branch at will simply by answering with a wrong accept key. By sizing the response so the header value ends at the tail of the buffer passed to websocket_connect() as wreq->tmp_buf, the peer can make the scan run off the end of that buffer and into adjacent memory. The defective log statement is compiled in only when websocket debug logging is enabled (CONFIG_NET_WEBSOCKET_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y, or CONFIG_LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL=4); it is absent from a default build, which bounds exposure to diagnostic configurations.

The consequence is an out-of-bounds read whose contents are emitted to the log stream: memory adjacent to the receive buffer is disclosed wherever the device's logs are collected or displayed. On targets where the memory following the buffer is not mapped, the scan can instead fault and terminate the connection or thread. No out-of-bounds write occurs, so there is no integrity impact.

The fix copies at most sizeof(got) - 1 bytes of the parser-provided slice into a bounded stack buffer, NUL terminates the copy, and logs that instead, so the formatter never reads beyond the bytes the parser actually offered.
CVE-2026-93671.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-93672.desc:
bt_att_find_req_by_user_data() in subsys/bluetooth/host/att.c walks every ATT channel attached to a connection and dereferences chan->req->user_data without checking chan->req. An ATT channel with no client request in flight holds chan->req == NULL — that is its normal idle state, set by att_handle_rsp() when a response resolves the transaction and tested by att_req_send_process() to pick a free channel — so the lookup reads through a NULL pointer as soon as it visits an idle channel. Every other chan->req user in the file already guards the pointer.

The lookup is reached from the public bt_gatt_cancel() API and, more importantly, from the host itself: bt_gatt_unsubscribe() calls bt_gatt_cancel() while a subscribe CCC write is still outstanding (BT_GATT_SUBSCRIBE_FLAG_WRITE_PENDING), and call_notify_cb_and_maybe_unsubscribe() in subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c invokes bt_gatt_unsubscribe() from the RX path whenever an application notify callback returns BT_GATT_ITER_STOP. A malicious or malfunctioning peer can hold the trigger window open by withholding the ATT Write Response to the CCC write and then sending a notification for the subscribed handle. With CONFIG_BT_EATT the traversal is very likely to meet an idle sibling channel, since ATT channels are prepended to the list and a channel opened after the pending request was sent is visited first.

The dereference is a read of a small constant offset from address zero, so the impact is availability only: no memory corruption, no attacker-chosen address and no information disclosure. On platforms and configurations where a near-NULL read traps — TrustZone non-secure images, MMU targets, native_sim, or builds with CONFIG_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION_DETECTION_MPU/_DWT — the fault occurs in the Bluetooth RX context and results in a fatal error and device reset. On a plain Cortex-M build with the vector table mapped at address 0 and null-pointer detection disabled (the default) the read succeeds and the defect is inert.

The fix adds an explicit chan->req != NULL test to the channel traversal and additionally rejects a NULL user_data argument, which would otherwise have matched, and cancelled, an unrelated request.
CVE-2026-93672.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-93673.desc:
The Zephyr WebSocket client validates the server's handshake response in on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c. The comparison was performed as strncmp(at, str, length), where length is the length of the value the server sent rather than the length of the expected value, so the check only asked whether the received value was a prefix of the expected base64(SHA-1(key || GUID)). A server that returned a handful of correct characters passed, and a response carrying an empty Sec-WebSocket-Accept: header caused strncmp() to be called with a count of zero, which returns 0 and set ctx->sec_accept_ok with no comparison performed at all. The header-value callback also cleared ctx->sec_accept_present after the first chunk, so a value split across receive-buffer boundaries was only ever examined in part.

ctx->sec_accept_ok is the sole WebSocket-specific gate in websocket_connect(); the client does not check the HTTP status code or the Upgrade:/Connection: headers. Any HTTP response containing an empty or prefix-matching Sec-WebSocket-Accept header therefore completed the handshake, after which the socket is finalized as a WebSocket and all further peer bytes are parsed as frames. The affected path is driven directly by remote input through subsys/net/lib/http/http_parser.c, and is reached by every user of websocket_connect(), including MQTT over WebSocket (subsys/net/lib/mqtt/mqtt_transport_websocket.c) and subsys/net/lib/ocpp/ocpp.c.

The Sec-WebSocket-Accept exchange is not a secret-based authentication -- an endpoint or on-path attacker that sees the request can compute the expected value -- so the impact is bounded to parties that never observed the handshake request: a caching or transparent intermediary replaying a canned response, an off-path attacker injecting a spoofed response, or a non-WebSocket endpoint the client was induced to talk to. For those, the per-connection binding that RFC 6455 requires the client to enforce provided no protection at all, letting a single crafted response convince the device it holds a live WebSocket session and causing it to send application data to, and accept frames from, an unverified peer. There is no memory-safety consequence.

The fix compares each delivered chunk against the expected value at the position reached so far, refuses a chunk that would overrun it, and accepts only once every byte of the expected value -- and no more -- has been matched; on_header_field() now also clears the flag for any other header so a partial value cannot be continued across an intervening header.
CVE-2026-93673.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-125275.title: A device certificate whose CA isn't registered can keep a TLS handshake running forever
CVE-2026-125275.desc:
Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in device certificate verification in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a TLS client certificate whose CA is not registered. When a client certificate chains to a root in the device endpoint's trust store but no CA in the chain is registered in NervesHub, NervesHub.SSL.decide/2 refuses it with the reason :unknown_ca. Erlang/OTP ssl reads that reason as a missing trust anchor, looks for an alternative root, finds the same root and validates again without end. The handshake process queries the database on each pass and keeps running after the client disconnects, until the node restarts.

The device endpoint trusts the public roots from CAStore unless DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE is set, so a client certificate from a public CA whose chain allows client authentication is sufficient. A chain that ends at a root outside the trust store is refused once.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.4.

CVE-2026-107493.title: Use-After-Free in PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() when appending to a caller-supplied stack fails
CVE-2026-107493.desc:
Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,
OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new
ones, but leaves them in the stack.

Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may
use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in
principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail,
but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and
OpenSSL itself does not do this.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and
private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO
structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the
function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are
already there unchanged.

If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack. This
includes the entries that were there before the call, and the entries
added by the call. It does not remove these entries from the stack, so
the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can happen at any
point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with invalid content
is enough.  This also happens if the stack was empty: entries added
before the failure are freed but stay in the stack.

An application that then reads or frees the stack will use memory that
was already freed. This can crash the application or, in principle,
corrupt memory.

Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are affected.
OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including the code that
TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When the stack is
NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created itself, which
is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an existing stack. An
attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data, but cannot make
an application pass an existing stack.

The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read()
and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code. OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
CVE-2026-107493.path: local access needed, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124709.title: Unbounded Memory Retention in QUIC Server for Rejected Streams
CVE-2026-124709.desc:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer
resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's
stream credit is returned.

Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly
open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the
process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming
stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks
the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is
collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected
stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends
RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never
sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.

The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default
stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as
the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams
the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy
explicitly are affected too.

Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit
window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection
open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without
bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived
connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
CVE-2026-124709.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-35190.desc:
Issue summary: A server configured with the Suite B certificate flag through
SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() and with TLS 1.3 enabled may read past the end of a
fixed group list when it processes a ClientHello whose supported_groups and
key_share contain no Suite B group.

Impact summary: A remote client can send a ClientHello that makes the server
read past the end of a static array. The values read are never returned to the
client, so no memory is disclosed; on builds with sanitizers or hardened
allocators the read may crash the process, causing Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: When the Suite B certificate flag is set, OpenSSL restricts the
accepted groups to P-256 and P-384 by substituting a fixed two-element list
for the configured group list. The tuple machinery used for key-share
selection was not updated for this substitution: tls1_get_group_tuples() still
returns the configured tuples, which by default describe eight groups. The
server-side walk in tls_parse_ctos_key_share() then advances through the
two-element list using those tuple counts without checking the cumulative
offset against the number of groups present.

Only applications that call SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() with
SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS and leave TLS 1.3 enabled are affected. The
openssl s_server -suiteB_128 option sets an X.509 verification parameter
instead, so the stock command line server is not vulnerable. Default
configurations do not reach this code.

A client that offers only groups outside the Suite B set, such as X25519,
forces every tuple to be walked and the read to run past the array. The bytes
read are compared against client group IDs and never sent back, so no memory
is disclosed. On builds with address sanitizers or hardened allocators the
read can abort the process; in ordinary release builds it reads a few bytes of
adjacent constant data.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
CVE-2026-35190.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-118498.desc: The CODESYS Automation Server Connector uses server-supplied file names without sufficient path traversal checks. An unauthenticated remote attacker controlling a malicious Automation Server and tricking a user to trust it, or performing a man-in-the-middle attack on a trusted communication channel, can exploit this vulnerability to write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary locations on the engineering workstation and subsequently achieve arbitrary code execution with user privileges.
CVE-2026-118498.path: remote, no login, needs user action

This Improper Authorization vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 7.1, allows an authenticated attacker to gain unintended access and can lead to the exposure of resources or functionality, possibly providing attackers with sensitive information or even execute arbitrary code.  	 	Atlassian recommends that Jira Service Management Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions: 		 		 Jira Service Management Data Center 10.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.3.27 		 		 Jira Service Management Data Center 11.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 11.3.13 		 		 	 	See the release notes (https://confluence.atlassian.com/servicemanagement/jira-service-management-release-notes-780083086.html). You can download the latest version of Jira Service Management Data Center from the download center (https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/service-management/download-archives).  	 	This vulnerability was reported via our Bug Bounty program.
CVE-2026-21609.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-119621.title: TYPO3 CMS - Path Traversal in Import/Export Module
CVE-2026-119621.desc: When importing a T3D or XML file in the Import/Export module, the file hash values of imported files were taken from the import data without validation and used to build the path of a temporary file. A crafted import file could therefore write files with arbitrary content to any location writable by the web server, for example a PHP file in the public web root, which leads to remote code execution. Exploiting this vulnerability requires an administrator backend user account, or a non-admin backend user for whom importing has been enabled via the user TSconfig option options.impexp.enableImportForNonAdminUser.
CVE-2026-119621.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-119622.title: TYPO3 CMS - Missing Authorization in Online Media Handling
CVE-2026-119622.desc:
The backend endpoint for adding online media (e.g. YouTube or Vimeo videos) accepted a target folder in the fallback storage (storage uid 0), which points to the public web root of the installation. File mount and permission checks are not applied to the fallback storage. As a result, any authenticated, low-privileged backend user, even without file mounts or module access, could create online media files with a partially controllable file name in the public web root.

In combination with TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-027, this could be used to re-enable the installer on an already configured instance. The installer could then be used to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution.
CVE-2026-119622.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-119623.title: TYPO3 CMS - Missing Authentication in Installer
CVE-2026-119623.desc:
The installer (first installation wizard) could be re-enabled on an already configured instance by placing a file whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL in the public web root or the project root. The installer then became accessible without authentication, allowing for example to change the database connection and to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution. As demonstrated in TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-026, such a file could be created by an authenticated, low-privileged backend user without any further permissions. Other ways of creating files in the web root, as well as leftover or restored marker files, could be abused in the same way.

With the fixed versions, the installer can no longer be re-enabled on an already configured instance by a marker file. A new internal setting $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SYS']['isInstalling'] is stored in the system configuration and is only enabled while a new installation is running. Additionally, only the exact file names FIRST_INSTALL and FIRST_INSTALL.txt are accepted as marker files.
CVE-2026-119623.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-125159.title: TYPO3 CMS - Information Disclosure in Image Processing
CVE-2026-125159.desc:
ImageMagick and GraphicsMagick use small modules, called "coders", to read each image format. When processing images, TYPO3 determined the coder from the file type detected by the file contents, as long as the detected mime-type started with image/. A file containing MVG (Magick Vector Graphics) instructions, uploaded with an image file extension like .png, was therefore processed with the MVG coder. MVG instructions can read local files into the processed image, which allows disclosing the contents of arbitrary files readable by the web server, for example configuration files containing credentials, through a publicly accessible processed image.

Exploiting this vulnerability requires a way to upload files without a mime-type check, for example a public form of the Form Framework using a FileUpload or ImageUpload element without configured allowedMimeTypes (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-032), which allows exploitation by unauthenticated visitors. Additionally, ImageMagick must be used for image processing, and its default system configuration must allow the MVG coder.
CVE-2026-125159.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-125160.desc:
Files uploaded through FileUpload or ImageUpload elements are stored in an unguessable sub-folder that remains the same for the whole form session. If storing an uploaded file failed, for example because of a file name exceeding the file system's length limit, the raw error message was shown to the frontend user disclosing the storage path including the unguessable folder name and the server's temporary upload directory. With this information, attackers could determine the public URL of files they upload through the form.

If a form allows uploading files that browsers can execute, such as HTML documents, this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder. This vulnerability is known to be actively exploited.
CVE-2026-125160.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-125161.desc: The fix for TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-009 was incomplete. GeneralUtility::sanitizeLocalUrl performed its checks on the URL-decoded value, but returned the original, URL-encoded value. URLs containing certain percent-encoded characters therefore passed the sanitization checks as local URLs, although they point to an external host. Applications that use the sanitized URL for redirects are vulnerable to open redirect attacks. This enables attackers to redirect users to external content and carry out phishing attacks. In the TYPO3 core, this affects redirects in the backend, which require the victim to be logged in to the backend.
CVE-2026-125161.path: remote, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-125162.title: TYPO3 CMS - Cache Flooding in Page Cache Handling
CVE-2026-125162.desc: The cHash argument, which ensures that only URL arguments originally generated by TYPO3 create separate page cache entries, was treated inconsistently when it was passed as an array. The cHash validation treated such a value as missing, while the page cache identifier treated it as present and included all URL arguments. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could create an unlimited number of page cache entries and trigger uncached page renderings by adding an array cHash with arbitrary values to any URL. This could exhaust server resources and fill the page cache storage. Only installations where the cHash validation is not enforced via $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['FE']['cacheHash']['enforceValidation'] are affected. This setting is enabled by default for new installations since TYPO3 v12, but is often still disabled in installations upgraded from older versions.
CVE-2026-125162.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-125163.desc: The FileUpload and ImageUpload elements of the Form Framework use the property allowedMimeTypes as an allow list of MIME types accepted for upload. An empty allowedMimeTypes list was treated as "no restriction". Forms containing upload elements without any configured MIME type, for example in manually created form definitions or when all MIME types were deselected in the form editor, accepted any file except those blocked by the file deny pattern, which only covers PHP-related file extensions. This allowed unauthenticated users to upload files with browser-executable content, such as HTML or SVG documents, to the configured upload folder, which by default is located in a public storage. If attackers know the URL of an uploaded file (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-029), this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder.
CVE-2026-125163.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-125164.desc: The file dump controller (eID=dumpFile) delivers files, file references and processed files identified by their uid, protected by a token. The token only covered the uid value, but not the type of the requested resource. A valid token issued for a file could therefore be reused to request a file reference or a processed file with the same uid. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could download files, for example from non-public storages, for which no token had been issued.
CVE-2026-125164.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-125165.desc: The RSS widget of the dashboard allows backend users to configure the URL of the RSS feed in the widget settings. The URL was fetched by the server without restricting the target host. Backend users with access to the dashboard could therefore make the server send HTTP requests to arbitrary hosts, including internal network services and cloud metadata endpoints, which are not reachable from the outside.
CVE-2026-125165.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-129273.title: N-central Audit Export syslog configuration injection allows root command execution

CVE-2026-129275.title: N-central ServerII2 repositoryItemGet missing authentication discloses any customer's automation policies

CVE-2026-129277.desc: N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the MaintActionGet operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can read and cancel the pending maintenance actions of any appliance.
CVE-2026-129277.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129278.desc: N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerII2 remoteControlMSPAStartEndTimeSubmit operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can alter the recorded state and times of Take Control remote control tasks and the associated audit log entries.
CVE-2026-129278.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129279.desc: The password reset function in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 returns distinguishable responses for valid and invalid accounts. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can enumerate the email addresses of valid user accounts.
CVE-2026-129279.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129280.title: N-central ServerUI and ServerUI2 SOAP operations missing authentication and authorisation allow cross-customer data access and modification
CVE-2026-129280.desc: Multiple ServerUI and ServerUI2 SOAP operations in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 do not verify the caller's session, permissions or customer scope. CVE-2026-129281.title: N-central ServerII2 incorrect authorisation allows view-only users to set DeviceExecute configuration run by Windows agents

CVE-2026-129282.title: N-central test email delivery sendmail argument injection with missing authorisation and CSRF protection

CVE-2026-129283.title: N-central custom service import XML external entity injection
CVE-2026-129283.desc: The custom service import in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 processes XML external entities. An authenticated attacker can upload a crafted service definition to read files accessible to the N-central service account or cause the server to make outbound requests.

CVE-2026-129284.desc: N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not validate connection targets in the Report Manager and Data Export settings. An authenticated attacker can cause the server to connect to arbitrary hosts, including loopback and internal addresses, and can use the responses to probe internal network services.
CVE-2026-129284.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-129285.desc: N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not verify that an action response received over XMPP originates from the appliance the request was sent to. An attacker with the credentials of one appliance can forge responses on behalf of another appliance.

CVE-2026-129286.title: N-central SIS GenericFiles version path traversal allows file write and remote code execution
CVE-2026-129286.desc: N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not validate version values and download locations in software update metadata. An attacker able to supply or modify the update metadata received by the server can write files outside the download directory and execute code as the N-central service account.

CVE-2026-129287.title: N-central SIS repository file parsers XML external entity injection
CVE-2026-129287.desc: N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 processes XML external entities in software repository files. An attacker able to supply or modify the repository files received by the server can read files accessible to the N-central service account or cause the server to make outbound requests.
CVE-2026-129287.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129448.title: Apache Roller Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
CVE-2026-129448.desc:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.
CVE-2026-129448.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2020-36323.desc: In the standard library in Rust before 1.52.0, there is an optimization for joining strings that can cause uninitialized bytes to be exposed (or the program to crash) if the borrowed string changes after its length is checked.
CVE-2020-36323.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-76463.desc:
As part of Cisco's ongoing commitment to proactive security and product quality, the Cisco networking engineering team has conducted a comprehensive internal security review. This review resulted in a software hardening release that addresses multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities.

The vulnerabilities tracked by CVE-2026-76463 are related to improper access control issues that are grouped under the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) CWE-284.
CVE-2026-76463.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-111590.desc: A wide range of Harbor versions allow SSRF via its webhook delivery component which does not properly validate web hook target addresses, allowing usage of private and link-local IP ranges. An authenticated attacker with ProjectAdmin permissions can configure a webhook policy pointing to a private internal address. When a project event fires, Harbor jobservice makes unauthenticated outbound HTTP POST requests to the target. If the target answers with an error status, the response body is written to the webhook execution log, which project members can read, potentially exposing cloud metadata or other network-restricted resources.
CVE-2026-111590.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-124643.title: Improper Authentication Vulnerability in e-Sushrut HMIS
CVE-2026-124643.desc:
This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to insufficient authentication and session validation in the dashboard functionality. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted HTTP requests to the affected endpoint.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to gain unauthorized access to the dashboard information associated with the targeted healthcare organization.
CVE-2026-124643.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124644.desc:
This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to the exposure of internal hospital operational statistics through data structure embedded in the HTML response of the login page. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by accessing the affected login page and extracting the returned HTML content.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to gain unauthorized access to internal hospital operational information associated with the targeted healthcare organization.
CVE-2026-124644.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124645.title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Key Vulnerability in e-Sushrut HMIS
CVE-2026-124645.desc:
This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HIMS due to the use of a static and predictable value in the client-side password hashing mechanism, which is embedded in the login page and accessible to unauthenticated users. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by accessing the login page, extracting the embedded value and using it to reproduce the password hashing process.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could weaken the security of the authentication mechanism and potentially facilitate authentication related attacks on the targeted healthcare organization.
CVE-2026-124645.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124646.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) Vulnerability in e-Sushrut HMIS
CVE-2026-124646.desc:
This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to insufficient server side object level authorization validation in the API endpoint. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by modifying the parameter value in the API request.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to enumerate and gain unauthorized access to sensitive information of patients on the targeted healthcare organization.
CVE-2026-124646.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-127138.desc:
pretix provides a mechanism where ticket QR codes are cryptographically signed and can be verified by our pretixSCAN apps in offline mode without any database of valid tickets. pretixSCAN checks the signature to verify that the ticket was issued by the correct pretix event and compares the QR code against a list of revoked QR codes. A QR code becomes revoked when the order is canceled, or the ticket is changed in a way that a new QR code needs to be generated.




However, the parsing of the QR code in all of our pretixSCAN apps contained a faulty computation, rendering the check for the correct length of the contents faulty. This way, an attacker is able to craft multiple QR codes for the same ticket which have the same content, but look different and therefore do not match against the revocation list. This does not allow to fabricate entirely new tickets, but it does allow to enter the event with e.g. a canceled ticket. This attack requires pretixSCAN to be scanning in offline mode and the "pretix signature scheme 1" to be used for the event's QR codes.




If the attack is executed, the ticket unfortunately shows as valid (green) on the scanner but as invalid (red) on the server since the server later cannot match it to a ticket. We scanned the entire database of scans on pretix Hosted and could not find any traces of this being exploited in the past.
CVE-2026-127138.path: local access needed, no login, needs user action

CVE-2026-127139.desc:
pretixSCAN Proxy does not use a secure random generator to generate initialization tokens and API keys for the connection between pretixSCAN devices and the pretixSCAN Proxy. This could allow a skilled attacker with access to at least some of the tokens to predict the value of other tokens more easily.




pretixSCAN is usually used on local networks and the level of exposure heavily depends on the structure of that network. If you want to be extra careful, it might make sense to reconnect your devices to the proxy after the update.
CVE-2026-127139.path: local access needed, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-127140.desc: Our WordPress plugin for the pretix Widget performs HTTP calls to pre-fetch CSS and JS files into a local cache and stores them publicly on the WordPress instance. These HTTP calls are made with wp_remote_get, not wp_safe_remote_get, and therefore allow SSRF with body extraction. Exploiting this requires sufficient WordPress permissions to create or modify pages.
CVE-2026-127140.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-127174.desc:
When changing the settings of a scheduled export, no permission checks are done to see whether the user making the change has access to the exporter after the change. This way, an attacker with access to change organizer settings and e.g. access to all orders could change the export to refer to gift cards instead, even if they do not have access to gift cards.




The fix for this is technically a breaking API change, since changing the export type of existing scheduled exports is no longer allowed, but we don't expect this to affect any typical API usage.
CVE-2026-127174.path: remote, needs admin rights, no user action

CVE-2026-12239.title: WP Abstracts <= 2.7.6 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Privilege Escalation via wpabs_save_regform AJAX Action
CVE-2026-12239.desc: The WP Abstracts plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.6. This is due to a missing capability check on the wpabs_save_regform AJAX action and the use of a static, frontend-exposed nonce that allows any authenticated user to persist attacker-controlled form schemas with arbitrary wpSync mappings that are later used as user meta keys in the wpabstracts_sync_wpfields function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to elevate their privileges to administrator.
CVE-2026-12239.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-130384.desc: Zammad before 7.2.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated customers to delete agents' shared ticket drafts by supplying a shared_draft_id. Attackers can create tickets via POST /api/v1/tickets or reply to accessible tickets referencing a draft id, destroying draft text prepared by agents.
CVE-2026-130384.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-107190.title: Path Traversal in Bludit
CVE-2026-107190.desc:
Bludit is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the page deletion functionality. An authenticated user with the Author role can set the UUID field of their own page to contain path traversal sequences (.. and path separators), which are saved without proper validation. When the page is deleted, Pages::delete() passes the path constructed from this UUID to Filesystem::deleteRecursive() without verifying that it still points to an allowed directory, allowing the attacker to delete any files, even not belonging to them. Critically, it is possible to delete admin pages and render the site unusable.


Because vendor contact attempts were unsuccessful, the vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.22.0 but may also affect other versions.
CVE-2026-107190.path: remote, needs a user login, needs user action

CVE-2026-130385.desc: Weblate 2026.11 through 2026.11.2 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the GET /api/tasks/{pk}/ endpoint that exposes unredacted repository error messages. Authenticated project members lacking vcs.view permission can poll failing repository tasks to obtain RepositoryCommandError text revealing upstream repository URLs, filesystem paths, and host names.
CVE-2026-130385.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-130386.desc: Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds access vulnerability in buffer_reclaim() and domain_set_free() in mpl.c that iterate the seed_set array one element past its end. Remote attackers can flood MPL multicast messages to fill the buffered message set, triggering out-of-bounds reads and writes of adjacent static memory that cause memory corruption or a crash.
CVE-2026-130386.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-130387.desc: Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in coap_remove_observer_by_uri() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read past the supplied URI buffer. Attackers can send a CoAP GET Observe request with a Uri-Path shorter than an existing observer's URL, causing memcmp with strlen to read beyond the non-NUL-terminated buffer.
CVE-2026-130387.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-130583.title: Rootways Authorize.net CIM Pro for Magento 2 before 4.1.5 SSRF via Apple Pay Validation
CVE-2026-130583.desc: Rootways Authorize.net CIM Pro extension for Magento 2 before 4.1.5 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Apple Pay merchant validation controller. Attackers can supply file://, gopher://, or dict:// URLs in the validationUrl parameter to read app/etc/env.php credentials and encryption keys or reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
products: Authorize.net CIM Pro extension for Magento 2
CVE-2026-130583.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-130584.title: Xibo CMS before 4.5.3 IDOR via /dataset/{id}/rss/{rssId}
CVE-2026-130584.desc: Xibo CMS before 4.5.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other DataSets' RSS feeds by pairing their own DataSet id with a foreign RSS id. Attackers with dataset.modify permission can read, edit, or delete feeds and steal PSKs, then use the unauthenticated /rss/{psk} endpoint to exfiltrate victim DataSet rows.
CVE-2026-130584.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-130587.title: OpenFunction through 1.2.0 Privilege Escalation via Unrestricted PodSpec Templates
CVE-2026-130587.desc: OpenFunction through 1.2.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows namespace tenants to create privileged host-access pods by supplying unrestricted PodSpec templates in Function and Serving resources. Attackers with only Function or Serving create permissions can set privileged, hostNetwork, hostPID, or hostPath fields to mount the worker node's root filesystem and escalate to node access.
CVE-2026-130587.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-130588.desc: OpenFunction through 1.2.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in getServingRun that allows users permitted to create Serving resources to crash the operator by omitting the triggers section. Attackers can submit a Serving with nil Spec.Triggers to crash-loop the controller-manager, halting Function and Serving reconciliation cluster-wide until the object is deleted.
CVE-2026-130588.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-130589.title: Emitter through 3.1 Master Key Forgery via Unauthenticated Channel Key Encryption
CVE-2026-130589.desc: Emitter through 3.1 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows any channel key holder to forge a master key because channel keys use bare XOR Salsa20 encryption without a MAC or signature. CVE-2026-130603.desc:

Truncated timestamp inputs can also cause out-of-bounds reads or assertion failures. A remote attacker able to deliver crafted timestamp-bearing Zenoh messages through an accepted transport can cause memory corruption and denial of service, with potential remote code execution in builds lacking appropriate binary protections. This issue is fixed in version 1.10.2.



Depending on the release and message-decoding path, the unchecked timestamp identifier length causes a heap-based or stack-based buffer overflow. Ordinary-frame network message decoding moved from heap-backed storage to stack-local storage in version 1.5.0. Earlier affected releases already contained stack-based decoding paths, including reassembled fragmented messages.

CVE-2026-130626.title: JDK HTTP client GET/DELETE follow cross-authority redirects with injected client, leaking API-key headers (POST-only gap)
CVE-2026-130626.desc: The core JDK HTTP client (a2a-java-sdk-http-client) applies the GHSA-9rhm redirect-neutralization only to the POST path. JdkGetBuilder.get(), JdkGetBuilder.getAsyncSSE(), and JdkDeleteBuilder.delete() call the injected httpClient directly, with no redirect gate. An application that supplies a redirect-capable HttpClient (Redirect.NORMAL/ALWAYS) — which is the SDK-documented way to enable POST redirects — silently follows cross-authority redirects on every credentialed GET/DELETE request. The JDK strips Authorization cross-origin, but forwards the four allowlisted custom credential headers (X-API-Key, API-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-Authentication) to the attacker-controlled authority. This is an incomplete-fix variant of GHSA-9rhm: the fix hardened the default client and added a POST-only two-step opt-in, but never covered GET/DELETE.
CVE-2026-130626.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-130627.title: Vert.x HTTP client forwards Authorization and all headers to cross-authority redirect target when followRedirects(true)
CVE-2026-130627.desc: The Vert.x HTTP client transport (a2a-java-sdk-http-client-vertx) hand-rolls a POST redirect follower that, when the documented PostBuilder.followRedirects(true) opt-in is enabled, re-issues the redirected request with the full request header map copied verbatim and performs no credential stripping and no same-authority check. A malicious, compromised, or mistyped agent that returns a 30x response with an absolute cross-host Location causes the client to forward the standard Authorization header (Bearer/Basic/OAuth) — plus every other header, including the allowlisted API-key headers — to the attacker-controlled authority. This breaks the project's own cross-transport invariant (SECURITY.md §8, OkHttpPostRedirectHeaderLeakTest) that credentials are stripped on cross-authority redirects even when redirects are followed. The sibling JDK and OkHttp/Android transports strip Authorization; Vert.x uniquely does not. This is a "fix introduced the bug" variant — the follower was added by the GHSA-9rhm hardening PR (3ae82912, refined by a5e76a0b).

CVE-2026-104100.title: Teable: Arbitrary root file write via attachment presign hash path traversal
CVE-2026-104100.desc: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.
CVE-2026-104100.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-110782.title: SAML2: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283: unsigned embedded Response bypasses HTTP-Artifact signature verification (no embedded-Issuer binding)
CVE-2026-110782.desc: The SimpleSAMLphp SAML2 library is a PHP library for SAML2 related functionality. From 6.2.2 until 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2, HTTPArtifact::receive() in src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php verifies a signed outer ArtifactResponse but returns an unsigned embedded SAML Response before calling verifyMessageSignature(). The signed path verifies with the artifact issuer's metadata keys without requiring the embedded Response issuer to match that artifact issuer. In a multi-IdP federation, an attacker controlling one trusted IdP can therefore return a validly signed outer ArtifactResponse containing an unsigned Response that claims a different IdP, bypassing the binding's embedded-message authentication. End-to-end impersonation requires a service provider using HTTP-Artifact and a downstream consumer that relies on the binding to authenticate the embedded Response rather than independently requiring a signature. This issue is fixed in versions 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2.
CVE-2026-110782.path: remote, no login, no user action

This Path Traversal (Arbitrary Read/Write) vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 7.7 and a CVSS Vector of CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose protected application configuration files, which has high impact to confidentiality, no impact to integrity, no impact to availability, and requires no user interaction.

Atlassian recommends that Crucible Server customers upgrade to the latest version. If you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to the specified supported fixed version:
 Crucible Server 4.9: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 4.9.16

The following description summarizes the vulnerability reported via our Penetration Testing program:

Crucible do not account for path parameters when validating protected paths requested through the static-resource route. A crafted path segment passes validation, after which Jetty removes the path parameter during dispatch and resolves the request to a protected resource. This can expose files under WEB-INF and permit direct invocation of admin-area JSPs outside the normal interceptor and administrative password checks. An ordinary authenticated user can exploit the issue, and unauthenticated exploitation is possible when anonymous access is enabled.

Prior to 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3, the Bluedroid BLE Mesh GATT server read handler bt_mesh_bta_gatts_cb in esp_ble_mesh stores a signed attribute-read callback length in an unsigned 16-bit variable. Prior to 17.0.0, the @libp2p/gossipsub default configuration allows a connected remote peer to submit unsigned subscription RPC metadata for arbitrarily many distinct topic strings. handleReceivedSubscription in packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts creates a persistent topics-map entry for each accepted topic, while allowedTopics is unset by default, decodeRpc maxSubscriptions limits only one RPC rather than aggregate topic bytes, and peer scoring has no subscription-volume penalty. CVE-2026-130621.title: Time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the local port selection in AWS efs-utils
CVE-2026-130621.desc:
A time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the local port selection in AWS efs-utils (amazon-efs-utils) before 3.3.5 might allow a user that can start EFS mounts on a shared host to read and write a different Amazon EFS or S3 Files file system that is mounted on that same host, under that mount's IAM identity and access point, via concurrent mount operations. Only file systems mounted on the same host at the same time can be affected. Every mount involved was configured by the owner of that host, using credentials and access points that owner controls, against file systems whose owners had already granted that host access, so the issue grants no access beyond what the host was already permitted and does not cross AWS account boundaries unless the host's owner configured a cross-account mount. The practical risk is lateral access between workloads on the same host at the same time, for example one container reading another container's file system under that container's identity. The issue does not expose the other mount's IAM credentials or TLS session keys.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade amazon-efs-utils to version 3.3.5 or later. Users of the Amazon EFS CSI Driver should upgrade to version 3.5.4 or later, and users of the Amazon EKS EFS CSI add-on should update to v3.5.4-eksbuild.1 or later.

CVE-2026-119292.title: FreeSWITCH late RTP/SRTP source validation permits one-way media starvation
CVE-2026-119292.desc: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, after FreeSWITCH has learned and closed source learning for an RTP peer, read_rtp_packet() and rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c reject RTP from an unrecognized source only after packet classification and, for encrypted calls, SRTP processing. An unauthenticated attacker with UDP reachability to an active RTP or SRTP media port can sustain a foreign-source packet flood that occupies the media read path and prevents legitimate media from entering FreeSWITCH on calls that consume incoming media for relay or echo. The resulting one-way audio allows the affected endpoint to continue hearing the other party, but the other party loses that endpoint's audio, leaving SIP signaling established while the call is unusable for conversation. Transmit-only playback was unaffected in testing. A caller can learn the media port from the SDP answer, while a third party must first discover an active port, and no valid SRTP key is required. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.
CVE-2026-119292.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-119293.title: FreeSWITCH RTP Inject and RTP Bleed during auto adjustment, plus SRTP media denial of service
CVE-2026-119293.desc: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. In 1.11.2 and earlier, rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c uses one session-wide autoadj_tally to learn RTP sources that differ from the address negotiated in SDP. An unauthenticated remote attacker who sends plaintext RTP during call setup can make packets from one or more non-advertised sources reach the threshold before the legitimate endpoint, causing FreeSWITCH to adopt the source of the threshold-crossing packet as the media peer. The attacker can then receive call audio, inject media, and deny media to the legitimate endpoint without being on the media path. FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 adds two opt-in controls, but both default to zero and the release remains affected unless both are configured before RTP session creation. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.11.2.
CVE-2026-119293.path: remote, no login, no user action

Decoding a non-matching untrusted string causes cubic regular expression backtracking, which can block the JavaScript event loop. The issue affects Schema.decodeUnknown, Schema.decodeUnknownSync, Schema.is, and consumers such as HttpApi and @effect/rpc payload decoding. This issue is fixed in version 3.22.1.
CVE-2026-121707.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-121716.title: fzf: Arbitrary command execution via bash arithmetic expansion on unvalidated layout size in fzf-tmux (-l/-u attached value)
CVE-2026-121716.desc: fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, bin/fzf-tmux validates separately supplied layout sizes but does not validate attached -l and -u layout values before Bash arithmetic expansion, allowing command substitution in a crafted operand to execute as the invoking user during option parsing. The same validation failure lets space-bearing popup geometry options -x, -y, -w, -h, and -p reach an unquoted tmux popup option string and inject additional tmux flags. Exploitation requires less-trusted project configuration, a wrapper, or a plugin to supply the poisoned value and requires the victim to invoke fzf-tmux; normal values are usually trusted, and the script has been superseded by built-in tmux options. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.

CVE-2026-121717.desc: fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, trigger-driven zsh completion in shell/completion.zsh uses _fzf_feed_fifo to create a FIFO at the predictable shared path ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fzf-complete-fifo-$$ and continues after removal or creation errors. On a multi-user host, a local attacker can pre-create that path as a symlink so the victim's completion stream overwrites a victim-writable file, potentially enabling code execution when that file is later sourced. A pre-created FIFO can instead disclose a bounded stream of completion candidates or block completion. On default modern hosts, fs.protected_symlinks blocks the overwrite variant, and protected_fifos and protected_regular further limit the FIFO disclosure and blocking variants, so exploitation depends on the relevant kernel protections being disabled and on the victim invoking the affected completion. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.
CVE-2026-121717.path: local access needed, needs a user login, needs user action

Without a shared cache, the attacker can affect only the attacker's own response. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

CVE-2026-128073.desc: gosaml2 is a Pure Go implementation of SAML 2.0. Prior to 0.12.0, ValidateEncodedResponse() calls decryptAssertions() on an EncryptedAssertion before signature or content validation completes, and EncryptedAssertion.DecryptBytes() in types/encrypted_assertion.go slices decoded ciphertext without first validating the required nonce or initialization-vector length. A CipherValue shorter than the 12-byte AES-GCM nonce causes a slice-bounds panic, and an empty AES-CBC CipherValue passes the modulo block-size check before causing a slice-bounds panic at the 16-byte initialization-vector split. An attacker needs only the service provider's public certificate to wrap a symmetric key, and no valid identity-provider signature or relationship is required. CVE-2026-95822.desc:
The SOCKS5 client in subsys/net/lib/socks/socks.c built the CONNECT request in socks5_tcp_connect() by choosing the SOCKS5 address type from the address family of the proxy (proxy->sa_family) while reading the bytes out of the destination address supplied to connect(). A SOCKS5 request encodes the destination independently of the transport used to reach the proxy, so the two families are unrelated and nothing in the path forces them to agree: set_context_proxy() only requires the proxy family to match the socket, and zsock_connect_ctx() enters the SOCKS branch before any destination validation. With an IPv6 proxy and an AF_INET destination the code treated an 8-byte struct net_sockaddr_in as a struct net_sockaddr_in6 and copied the 16-byte sin6_addr from it, reading 12 bytes past the end of the object and transmitting them to the proxy.

With CONFIG_USERSPACE enabled, z_vrfy_zsock_connect() copies only addrlen user bytes into a stack-resident struct net_sockaddr_storage and enforces no per-family minimum length, so the oversized read stays within the storage but returns stale, uninitialised kernel-stack bytes. An unprivileged user-mode thread can therefore open an AF_INET6 stream socket, point setsockopt(SO_SOCKS5) at a proxy it controls, and call connect() with a short AF_INET destination to have the kernel send it 12 bytes of supervisor stack residue per attempt. Without CONFIG_USERSPACE the read runs past the end of the caller's own struct net_sockaddr_in, disclosing adjacent memory to the proxy; the family mismatch can arise unintentionally when a destination is obtained from DNS while an IPv6 proxy is configured.

Impact is limited to information disclosure of at most 12 bytes per connect() call, with no write primitive; the leak is delivered to whoever operates the SOCKS5 proxy. The mirrored pairing (IPv6 destination through an IPv4 proxy) is memory-safe but encoded the destination as SOCKS5_ATYP_IPV4 from the first four bytes of the IPv6 address, causing the proxy to connect to an unrelated host. Exploitation requires the non-default CONFIG_SOCKS option, a socket with SO_SOCKS5 configured, and both IPv4 and IPv6 support in the image.

The fix moves the encoding into a helper that selects the address type from dest->sa_family and validates dest_len against the matching struct net_sockaddr_in/struct net_sockaddr_in6 before copying, rejecting under-length or unsupported destinations with an error.
CVE-2026-95822.path: local access needed, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2026-97698.title: Mistune: Quadratic-time DoS in parse_link_href via unbounded parenthesis scan on empty-label links
CVE-2026-97698.desc: Mistune is a Python Markdown parser with renderers and plugins. Prior to 3.3.4, parse_link_href performs an unbounded parenthesis-balancing scan to the end of the document for each unmatched opening parenthesis reached through an empty [] link label. In src/mistune/helpers.py and src/mistune/inline_parser.py, the empty label bypasses no_close_bracket_before, and no_link_before advances only past the short label, so successive [] ( candidates repeatedly scan the remaining document. Rendering untrusted Markdown with the default HTML renderer and no plugins can perform quadratic CPU work and keep a worker at 100 percent utilization. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.4.
CVE-2026-97698.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-97699.title: Mistune: Quadratic-time DoS in inline image parsing (precedence_scan) bypasses not-is-image guards
CVE-2026-97699.desc: Mistune is a Python Markdown parser with renderers and plugins. Prior to 3.3.4, inline image parsing sends nested ![ openers through precedence_scan because the no_link_before and _label_contains_link linearization guards are gated by not is_image. In src/mistune/inline_parser.py, each outer image opener can therefore search the remaining image body, while max_image_depth does not apply because the failed scans do not produce image tokens. Rendering untrusted Markdown with the default HTML renderer and no plugins can perform quadratic CPU work and keep a worker at 100 percent utilization. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.4.
CVE-2026-97699.path: remote, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-14265.title: AWS-advanced-jdbc-wrapper: Java Deserialization RCE via Cache Poisoning
CVE-2026-14265.desc:
### Impact
The AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper is an open-source JDBC driver wrapper that extends a JDBC driver to enable Amazon Aurora and AWS Cloud features such as failover handling and caching. We identified CVE-2026-14265, an issue in the RemoteQueryCachePlugin of the AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper. When this plugin is enabled, query results read from the shared Redis/Valkey cache are deserialized without class filtering. An actor with write access to the shared cache infrastructure could insert a crafted serialized Java object that, when read by an application, results in execution of arbitrary code on the application server.

### Workarounds
The RemoteQueryCachePlugin is not enabled by default. Customers who cannot immediately upgrade can mitigate this issue by disabling the RemoteQueryCachePlugin, and by restricting write access to the Redis/Valkey cache infrastructure to trusted principals.
CVE-2026-14265.path: remote, needs a user login, no user action

CVE-2025-62165.title: Pi-hole FTL: WebUI (& API) DoS mechanism - Lack of rate limiting : Silent CPU consumption and/or Log file expansion
CVE-2025-62165.desc: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, CivetWeb permits unauthenticated clients to flood the WebUI login page and API invalid paths without connection or request-rate limits. Repeated requests can consume substantial CPU in request processing and session authentication, making the WebUI sluggish or unresponsive and potentially affecting the wider system and DNS service. Requests to selected invalid or redirecting paths also generate a log entry for each request, allowing network traffic to expand logs and exhaust constrained storage such as an SD card, while other request forms consume CPU without producing a corresponding request log. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.7.

CVE-2026-102529.title: HtmlSanitizer: CSS Removal DoS
CVE-2026-102529.desc: HtmlSanitizer is a .NET library for cleaning HTML fragments and documents from constructs that can lead to XSS attacks. Prior to 9.0.967 and 9.1.968-beta, HtmlSanitizer CSS style-declaration sanitization can process an attacker-controlled style attribute with quadratic cost because SanitizeStyleDeclaration repeatedly causes the complete declaration to be serialized while removing disallowed CSS properties. One unauthenticated request can occupy a synchronous application worker for seconds, and concurrent requests can saturate all workers and sustain denial of service. This issue is fixed in versions 9.0.967 and 9.1.968-beta.
