CVE-2026-129807.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129808.title: EoE Buffer Callback NULL Pointer Dereference
CVE-2026-129808.desc: The EoE receive and transmit paths call the handle_recv_buffer and fetch_send_buffer callbacks without first checking whether they are set. Both callbacks are documented as optional; an application that omits either one causes a call through a NULL function pointer when the first EoE frame arrives or when the transmit polling loop runs.
CVE-2026-129808.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129809.title: FoE Unconfigured Access NULL Pointer Dereference
CVE-2026-129809.desc: ESC_foeprocess can be reached by an incoming mailbox frame before the application calls FOE_config to supply the file table and flush buffer pointers. When foe_cfg or its fbuffer field is NULL the handler dereferenced those pointers while processing the frame, causing a NULL pointer dereference.
CVE-2026-129809.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129810.title: EoE Unconfigured Access NULL Pointer Dereference
CVE-2026-129810.desc: ESC_eoeprocess and ESC_eoeprocess_tx can be reached before the application calls EOE_config to supply the callback table pointer. When eoe_cfg is NULL the receive handler dereferenced it while processing an incoming EoE frame, and the transmit polling function dereferenced it on each cycle, causing NULL pointer dereferences.
CVE-2026-129810.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129811.title: CoE PDO Mapping Size Exceeds Process Data Buffer Out-of-Bounds Write
CVE-2026-129811.desc: The PDO mapping bit lengths stored in the mapping objects are writable by the master via SDO. sizeOfPDO summed them without checking the total against the size of the rxpdo[] or txpdo[] process data buffers. A master can craft a mapping whose total bit count exceeds those buffers, causing COE_pdoPack and COE_pdoUnpack to write past their ends during each process data cycle after the PREOP to SAFEOP transition.
CVE-2026-129811.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129812.title: CoE PDO Mapping of Dataless Entry NULL Pointer Dereference
CVE-2026-129812.desc: An object dictionary entry that holds a constant has no process data storage and carries a NULL data pointer. sizeOfPDO did not check for this when resolving a mapped entry to its descriptor. A master that maps such an entry to a PDO causes COE_pdoPack or COE_pdoUnpack to dereference the NULL data pointer on every process data exchange after the mapping is activated.
CVE-2026-129812.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129813.title: CoE Complete Access Download to Dataless Entry NULL Pointer Dereference
CVE-2026-129813.desc: The CoE complete-access download handler iterated over all subindices of an object and wrote the master-supplied payload into each writable entry. Entries that hold a constant have write-access flags set but carry a NULL data pointer. The handler did not check for this and wrote the master payload through the NULL pointer.
CVE-2026-129813.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-129814.title: CoE Object Name Null Terminator Off-by-One Out-of-Bounds Write
CVE-2026-129814.desc: The SDO Information Get Object Description and Get Entry Description responses copy the object or entry name into the mailbox data area and then write a null terminator byte. The copy loops ran up to the last available byte in the buffer, leaving no room for the terminator. When an object or entry name exactly fills the available space the terminator is written one byte past the end of the mailbox data buffer.
CVE-2026-129814.path: adjacent network, no login, no user action

CVE-2026-124626.title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass via empty route parameters and wildcards
CVE-2026-124626.desc: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. CVE-2026-129850.title: @fastify/express vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via Unicode case folding

CVE-2026-133312.desc: @fastify/rate-limit is the rate-limiting plugin for the Fastify web framework. Because the peek and the consume are two separate store operations with the password check in between, concurrent requests can all pass the peek before any slot is consumed, so in versions 11.1.0 through 11.2.2 a burst of requests runs far more failed attempts than the configured limit, and the sequential path also allowed one attempt more than configured. The default per-request limiter is not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/rate-limit 11.3.0, which makes the manual flow atomic by reserving a slot in a single operation and refunding it only on success, and users should upgrade to 11.3.0 or later.

CVE-2026-125294.title: Nexter Blocks Pro <= 5.0.10 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Unicode Collation Confusion in 'tpgb_acf_key' Parameter
CVE-2026-125294.desc: The Nexter Blocks Pro plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.10 via the `tpgb_ajax_register_user()` function. This is due to a byte-level denylist on the `tpgb_acf_key[]` and `tpgb_acf[]` parameters that fails to block Unicode look-alike characters — such as U+1E87 and U+00E7 in a key like `ẇp_çapabilities` — whose UTF-8 byte sequences do not match any ASCII-based pattern check, while the database's default accent-insensitive collation (`utf8mb4_unicode_ci` / `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`) treats the decorated key as equivalent to the canonical `wp_capabilities` row, causing `update_user_meta()` to overwrite the newly registered user's role with `administrator`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to register a new account bearing the full Administrator role, gaining complete control over the WordPress site including the ability to install plugins, modify files, and execute arbitrary code. The nonce required by the handler is publicly emitted on any page containing the tp-login-register block, making the full exploit chain — nonce retrieval, a single crafted registration POST, and the plugin's own `autologin` flow — trivially reachable on any default install where user registration is enabled. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.
CVE-2026-125294.path: remote, no login, no user action
